{"ops": [{"op": "replace", "target": {"kind": "blocks", "ids": ["mgkg4ysewx9.47"]}, "with": {"from": {"kind": "inline", "content": "## Leveling activities

Both of your ideas are strong and work best with different jobs: toys are the steady, easy source of XP and growth, and bugs are the exciting hunt that targets specific stats.

**Toy drops.** The plot's toy dispenser drops a random toy on a timer. Players place toys for the blob to play with, giving XP and growth. Toys come in tiers (squeaky ball, yarn, rocket toy) so better toys grow blobs faster.

**Bug catching.** Bugs spawn around the map outside the plots, with rarer bugs in harder spots or at night. Players catch them with a net and feed them to their blob for bonus points in one stat.

| Bug tier | Example | Reward |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common | Beetle | Small XP |
| Uncommon | Firefly | +1 Speed |
| Rare | Stag beetle | +1 Melee |
| Epic | Glowmoth | +1 Range or Health |
| Legendary | Crystal mantis | +1 stat point of the player's choice |

**Other ideas worth adding:**

- **Daily quests.** Three small tasks a day (catch 5 bugs, win a dungeon floor) for coins and XP. Keeps players returning.
- **Food.** From the berry garden; the main growth source alongside toys.
- **Offline growth.** Blobs gain a small amount of XP while the player is away, capped at a few hours, so logging back in always feels rewarding."}, "as": "markdown"}}]}

{"ops": [{"op": "replace", "target": {"kind": "blocks", "ids": ["mgkg4ysewx9.48"]}, "with": {"from": {"kind": "inline", "content": "## Combat

All battles use one combat system: the player rides their blob on a saddle and fights with movement, melee, ranged attacks and a dash. Dungeons and wager wars are just different opponents and rewards on top of it.

**Riding.** A basic saddle is free with the first blob; fancier saddles are cosmetics. The player sits on the blob, and the blob's Speed stat sets how fast they move.

**Controls (PC / mobile buttons):**

| Action | PC | Uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | WASD | Speed |
| Melee hit | Left click | Melee, small Stamina |
| Ranged shot | Right click or E | Range, small Stamina |
| Dash | Shift | Speed and Melee, large Stamina |
| Special ability | Q | Ability Power, cooldown |

Arenas have cover, ramps and hazards so skilled movement beats raw stats. Every control needs an on-screen button for mobile players, who are a large share of Roblox.

**Dungeon floors 1 to 20.** AI bosses get tougher each floor. Players must clear a floor to unlock the next, and first clears pay a bonus.

| Floors | Difficulty | Idea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1–5 | Easy | Teach the controls, one simple attack each |
| 6–10 | Medium | Bosses that dodge and shoot back |
| 11–15 | Hard | Arena hazards, boss minions |
| 16–19 | Very hard | Multi-phase bosses |
| 20 | Nearly impossible | Final boss; huge reward and a rare cosmetic |

**Wager wars.** In the center arenas, two players (or two teams of two) agree on a coin wager, both confirm, and the winner takes the pot. Both see each other's blob level before accepting. Keep wagers to coins earned in play and never to anything bought with Robux (see Shops and monetization)."}, "as": "markdown"}}]}

{"ops": [{"op": "replace", "target": {"kind": "blocks", "ids": ["mgkg4ysewx9.49"]}, "with": {"from": {"kind": "inline", "content": "## Shops and monetization

Three shops cover your plan: cosmetic chests and farm decor for coins, and a Robux shop for boosts and convenience. Roblox requires that any random item bought with Robux, or with currency that can be bought with Robux, shows every possible outcome and its exact odds before purchase ([Roblox policy](https://create.roblox.com/docs/production/monetization/paid-random-items)).

**1. Cosmetic chest shop (coins).** Chests roll a random item for the blob: hats, shirts, tuxedos, auras, saddle skins. Show the full item list and odds on each chest, even if coins can't be bought, since it's required the moment you sell coins for Robux.

**2. Farm decor shop (coins).** Direct purchases, no randomness: lights, trees, flowers, paths, fences, fountains, plot themes.

**3. Robux shop.**

| Item | Type | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2x Money | Game pass | Double coins from all sources |
| 2x Luck | Game pass | Better egg and chest odds; the odds screen must update to show the boosted odds |
| 2x Growth | Game pass | Double XP and growth |
| 4th pet slot | Game pass | Unlocks slot 4 |
| Auto-feeder | Game pass | Feeds blobs from stored food while away |
| VIP | Game pass | Chat tag, rainbow name sign on the plot, exclusive decor |
| Coin packs | Developer product | Instant coins |
| Stat respec token | Developer product | Reset a blob's stat points |
| Instant hatch / toy refill | Developer product | Skip wait timers |
| Exclusive cosmetics | Developer product | Direct-buy outfits and auras, no randomness |

**Keep wager wars fair.** If coins can be bought with Robux, wagering them comes close to gambling. Two safer options: give wager wars their own currency (trophies) that can only be earned, or turn off Robux boosts inside wager arenas. Paid boosts are fine in dungeons and growth, but buying wins against friends drives players away."}, "as": "markdown"}}]}

input.payload:
{"ops": [{"op": "replace", "target": {"kind": "blocks", "ids": ["mgkg4ysewx9.50"]}, "with": {"from": {"kind": "inline", "content": "## My take

The concept is strong, and the best part is riding your own blob into skill-based fights. Most pet games have pets that just follow you, so that is what will make this one stand out. The biggest risk is scope: 1.1 as written is a lot, so ship it in phases.

**Strongest ideas:**

- **Riding battles with real movement.** Your hook. Put the most polish here.
- **Growing from tiny to full size.** Very satisfying to watch, and it makes each blob feel personal.
- **Choosing stat points.** Gives players identity ("my blob is a speed build").
- **Dungeon floors 1 to 20.** A clear long-term goal with a bragging-rights final floor.
- **Bugs for specific stats.** Turns grinding into a collection hunt.

**Risks to plan for:**

- **Scope.** Release once phases 1 to 5 work, then add the rest as updates. Regular updates also bring players back.
- **Data saving.** Lost progress kills games. Use a proven saving setup from day one and test it often.
- **Mobile controls.** Combat must feel good on a phone, not just with a keyboard.
- **Pay-to-win in PvP and odds rules.** Covered in Shops; decide early, since it's hard to change once players have spent Robux.

**Open questions:**

- [ ] What resets on rebirth, and what carries over?
- [ ] How many stat points per level?
- [ ] Can blobs faint in battle, and what does losing cost?
- [ ] Will players be able to trade blobs? (Trading adds rules if items came from paid random rolls.)
- [ ] How many blob types at launch? 4 to 6 is a good starting set.
- [ ] Names for the currencies."}, "as": "markdown"}}]}

The foundation is three scripts. Here's where each one goes in Roblox Studio:

| File | Where it goes | Type to insert |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BlobDefinitions.lua | ReplicatedStorage | **ModuleScript**, named `BlobDefinitions` |
| DataManager.lua | ServerScriptService | **ModuleScript**, named `DataManager` |
| PlayerSetup.server.lua | ServerScriptService | **Script**, named `PlayerSetup` |

The names matter, because the scripts find each other by name. Your PlotManager script stays where it is.

**Two settings before testing (saving won't work without them):**
1. Publish your game: **File → Publish to Roblox**.
2. **File → Game Settings → Security**, turn on **Enable Studio Access to API Services**.

**How to test it:**
Press Play and open the **Output** window (View → Output). You'll see your save printed with 100 coins and a test blob called Bouncer. Stop, press Play again, and you should have 200 coins and the same blob with a higher level. If the numbers carry over, saving works.

**What each piece does:**
- **BlobDefinitions** is the one list of every blob type: stats, size, movement style, rarity. I made four placeholders (Bouncer, Roller, Hopper, Wobbler) that you can rename or change. Adding a new blob later just means copying one entry.
- **DataManager** loads and saves everything: coins, rebirths, blobs, inventory, and progress. It has protections so players can't lose their progress, like kicking with a "please rejoin" message instead of giving them blank data if Roblox's servers have a hiccup.
- **PlayerSetup** shows Coins and Rebirths on the leaderboard, and runs the test while you're in Studio. Set `TEST_MODE = false` before you release the game.

Two details to be aware of: rebirths currently keep blobs and stats (my assumption from the doc), and the 4th-slot game pass ID is set to 0 until you create the pass.

Once you've confirmed saving works, the next step is phase 2: an egg stand and making a blob appear and follow you on your plot. Do you want to make the first blob model yourself, or should I build a simple one from parts?

--[[
	BlobDefinitions (ModuleScript)
	Put this in ReplicatedStorage so both the server and players' UI can read it.

	This is the ONE place that describes every blob type in the game.
	To add a new blob later, copy one entry in Blobs, give it a new key,
	and change its numbers. Everything else in the game reads from here.
]]

local BlobDefinitions = {}

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STATS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The order here is the order they show up in the stat screen.
BlobDefinitions.StatOrder = { "Health", "Stamina", "Melee", "Range", "Speed", "AbilityPower" }

-- How much ONE stat point adds to each stat
BlobDefinitions.StatPerPoint = {
	Health       = 10,
	Stamina      = 5,
	Melee        = 2,
	Range        = 2,
	Speed        = 0.5,
	AbilityPower = 3,
}

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- RARITIES
---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Weight = how often this rarity is rolled compared to the others.
-- Only Common blobs exist right now; the others are ready for later.
BlobDefinitions.Rarities = {
	Common    = { Order = 1, Color = Color3.fromRGB(190, 190, 190) },
	Uncommon  = { Order = 2, Color = Color3.fromRGB(85, 200, 90) },
	Rare      = { Order = 3, Color = Color3.fromRGB(70, 140, 255) },
	Epic      = { Order = 4, Color = Color3.fromRGB(170, 85, 255) },
	Legendary = { Order = 5, Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 180, 40) },
}

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- GROWTH & LEVELING
---------------------------------------------------------------------
BlobDefinitions.HatchSize       = 0.4 -- blobs hatch at 40% of full size
BlobDefinitions.PointsPerLevel  = 1   -- stat points gained each level
BlobDefinitions.MaxLevel        = 100

-- XP needed to go from `level` to `level + 1`
function BlobDefinitions.XPToNextLevel(level)
	return math.floor(50 * level ^ 1.5)
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- BLOB TYPES
---------------------------------------------------------------------
--[[
	Placeholder blobs — rename them and change their numbers freely.

	DisplayName     : name players see
	Rarity          : one of the Rarities above
	MovementStyle   : how it moves on the plot (Bounce, Roll, Hop, Wobble, Slither, Hover)
	FullSize        : height in studs when fully grown
	FullGrowthLevel : level where it reaches full size; after this only stats grow
	BaseStats       : starting stats before any points are spent
	ModelName       : name of its model in ReplicatedStorage.BlobModels (we'll add models later)
]]
BlobDefinitions.Blobs = {
	Bouncer = {
		DisplayName = "Bouncer",
		Description = "A springy blob that never stops bouncing.",
		Rarity = "Common",
		MovementStyle = "Bounce",
		FullSize = 6,
		FullGrowthLevel = 20,
		BaseStats = { Health = 100, Stamina = 50, Melee = 10, Range = 8, Speed = 16, AbilityPower = 10 },
		ModelName = "Bouncer",
	},

	Roller = {
		DisplayName = "Roller",
		Description = "Curls into a ball and rolls everywhere it goes.",
		Rarity = "Common",
		MovementStyle = "Roll",
		FullSize = 5,
		FullGrowthLevel = 20,
		BaseStats = { Health = 90, Stamina = 60, Melee = 12, Range = 6, Speed = 18, AbilityPower = 10 },
		ModelName = "Roller",
	},

	Hopper = {
		DisplayName = "Hopper",
		Description = "Takes big leaps like a frog.",
		Rarity = "Common",
		MovementStyle = "Hop",
		FullSize = 5.5,
		FullGrowthLevel = 20,
		BaseStats = { Health = 85, Stamina = 55, Melee = 8, Range = 12, Speed = 17, AbilityPower = 10 },
		ModelName = "Hopper",
	},

	Wobbler = {
		DisplayName = "Wobbler",
		Description = "Slow and wobbly, but very tough.",
		Rarity = "Common",
		MovementStyle = "Wobble",
		FullSize = 7,
		FullGrowthLevel = 20,
		BaseStats = { Health = 130, Stamina = 45, Melee = 11, Range = 7, Speed = 14, AbilityPower = 10 },
		ModelName = "Wobbler",
	},
}

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- HELPERS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
function BlobDefinitions.Get(blobType)
	return BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobType]
end

function BlobDefinitions.Exists(blobType)
	return BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobType] ~= nil
end

-- Size multiplier (0.4 → 1.0) for a blob at a given level
function BlobDefinitions.GetSizeScale(blobType, level)
	local def = BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobType]
	if not def then return 1 end
	local progress = math.clamp((level - 1) / (def.FullGrowthLevel - 1), 0, 1)
	return BlobDefinitions.HatchSize + (1 - BlobDefinitions.HatchSize) * progress
end

-- Final value of one stat for a saved blob: base + spent points + bug bonuses
function BlobDefinitions.GetStat(blobData, statName)
	local def = BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobData.Type]
	if not def then return 0 end
	local base = def.BaseStats[statName] or 0
	local spent = (blobData.Allocated and blobData.Allocated[statName]) or 0
	local bonus = (blobData.Bonus and blobData.Bonus[statName]) or 0
	return base + (spent + bonus) * (BlobDefinitions.StatPerPoint[statName] or 0)
end

-- All final stats at once, as a table
function BlobDefinitions.GetAllStats(blobData)
	local result = {}
	for _, statName in ipairs(BlobDefinitions.StatOrder) do
		result[statName] = BlobDefinitions.GetStat(blobData, statName)
	end
	return result
end

return BlobDefinitions

--[[
	DataManager (ModuleScript)
	Put this in ServerScriptService.

	Loads, saves and changes each player's data. Every other server script
	should go through this module instead of touching DataStores directly.

	Safety features:
	  • Session lock: a player's data can only be open on one server at a time,
	    so joining a new server quickly can't overwrite newer progress.
	  • Retries when Roblox's DataStores have a hiccup.
	  • If data can't be loaded, the player is kicked instead of being given
	    blank data (which would wipe their real save).
	  • Autosave every 2 minutes, save on leave, save on server shutdown.

	Main functions:
	  DataManager.Get(player)              → their data table (nil if not loaded)
	  DataManager.WaitForData(player)      → waits until loaded, then returns data
	  DataManager.Loaded                   → event fired (player, data) once loaded
	  DataManager.AddCoins(player, amount)
	  DataManager.SpendCoins(player, amount) → true if they could afford it
	  DataManager.GetMaxSlots(player)
	  DataManager.AddBlob(player, blobType) → new blob data, or nil + reason
	  DataManager.AddXP(player, blobId, amount)
	  DataManager.SpendStatPoint(player, blobId, statName)
]]

local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")
local MarketplaceService = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local BlobDefinitions = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BlobDefinitions"))

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SETTINGS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local STORE_NAME        = "BlobGame_PlayerData_v1" -- change the version to start everyone fresh
local AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL = 120   -- seconds
local LOAD_ATTEMPTS     = 6
local RETRY_DELAY       = 5     -- seconds between load attempts
local LOCK_TIMEOUT      = 1800  -- a lock older than 30 min is treated as abandoned

local BASE_SLOTS          = 1
local MAX_REBIRTH_SLOTS   = 2   -- rebirths 1 and 2 each give a slot
local EXTRA_SLOT_PASS_ID  = 0   -- put your 4th-slot game pass ID here once you make it

-- Every new player starts with this. Adding a new field here
-- automatically adds it to existing players' saves too.
local TEMPLATE = {
	DataVersion = 1,
	Coins = 0,
	Rebirths = 0,
	Blobs = {},              -- [blobId] = blob data
	EquippedBlobId = "",     -- the blob that follows / fights; "" = none
	Inventory = {
		Food = {},           -- [itemName] = count
		Toys = {},
		Bugs = {},
		Cosmetics = {},
		Decor = {},
	},
	Progress = {
		TotalHatched = 0,
		HighestDungeonFloor = 0,
		WagerWins = 0,
		WagerLosses = 0,
	},
}

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- INTERNALS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore(STORE_NAME)
local profiles = {}   -- [player] = data
local saving = {}     -- [player] = true while a save is running

local loadedEvent = Instance.new("BindableEvent")

local DataManager = {}
DataManager.Loaded = loadedEvent.Event

local function deepCopy(t)
	local copy = {}
	for k, v in pairs(t) do
		copy[k] = type(v) == "table" and deepCopy(v) or v
	end
	return copy
end

-- Fills in any fields that are missing from an older save
local function reconcile(data, template)
	for k, v in pairs(template) do
		if data[k] == nil then
			data[k] = type(v) == "table" and deepCopy(v) or v
		elseif type(v) == "table" and type(data[k]) == "table" and k ~= "Blobs" then
			reconcile(data[k], v)
		end
	end
end

local function keyFor(player)
	return "Player_" .. player.UserId
end

-- Mirrors values the client should see onto player attributes
local function syncAttributes(player, data)
	player:SetAttribute("Coins", data.Coins)
	player:SetAttribute("Rebirths", data.Rebirths)
	player:SetAttribute("EquippedBlobId", data.EquippedBlobId)
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- LOADING
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function loadData(player)
	local key = keyFor(player)

	for attempt = 1, LOAD_ATTEMPTS do
		local force = attempt == LOAD_ATTEMPTS -- last try: take over a stuck lock
		local blockedByLock = false
		local loaded

		local ok, err = pcall(function()
			store:UpdateAsync(key, function(old)
				blockedByLock = false
				local data = old or deepCopy(TEMPLATE)
				local lock = data.SessionLock

				if not force and lock and lock.JobId ~= game.JobId
					and os.time() - lock.Time < LOCK_TIMEOUT then
					blockedByLock = true
					return nil -- cancel: another server still has this player open
				end

				data.SessionLock = { JobId = game.JobId, Time = os.time() }
				loaded = data
				return data
			end)
		end)

		if ok and not blockedByLock and loaded then
			reconcile(loaded, TEMPLATE)
			return loaded
		end

		if not ok then
			warn(("[DataManager] Load attempt %d failed for %s: %s"):format(attempt, player.Name, tostring(err)))
		else
			warn(("[DataManager] %s's data is open on another server, retrying (%d/%d)")
				:format(player.Name, attempt, LOAD_ATTEMPTS))
		end

		if not player.Parent then return nil end -- they left while we waited
		task.wait(RETRY_DELAY)
	end

	return nil
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SAVING
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function saveData(player, releaseLock)
	local data = profiles[player]
	if not data then return end

	-- Wait if another save for this player is still running
	while saving[player] do task.wait() end
	saving[player] = true

	data.SessionLock = releaseLock and nil or { JobId = game.JobId, Time = os.time() }

	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		store:UpdateAsync(keyFor(player), function(old)
			-- Another server took over this player's data: don't overwrite it
			if old and old.SessionLock and old.SessionLock.JobId ~= game.JobId then
				return nil
			end
			return data
		end)
	end)

	if not ok then
		warn(("[DataManager] Save failed for %s: %s"):format(player.Name, tostring(err)))
	end

	saving[player] = nil
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- PLAYER JOIN / LEAVE
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
	local data = loadData(player)

	if not data then
		player:Kick("We couldn't load your save. Please rejoin in a minute — your progress is safe.")
		return
	end
	if not player.Parent then return end -- left during loading

	profiles[player] = data

	-- Check the extra-slot game pass once per join
	if EXTRA_SLOT_PASS_ID ~= 0 then
		local ok, owns = pcall(MarketplaceService.UserOwnsGamePassAsync, MarketplaceService, player.UserId, EXTRA_SLOT_PASS_ID)
		player:SetAttribute("HasExtraSlotPass", ok and owns or false)
	end

	syncAttributes(player, data)
	player:SetAttribute("DataLoaded", true)
	loadedEvent:Fire(player, data)
end

local function onPlayerRemoving(player)
	saveData(player, true)
	profiles[player] = nil
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(onPlayerRemoving)
for _, player in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
	task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, player)
end

-- Autosave
task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		task.wait(AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL)
		for player in pairs(profiles) do
			task.spawn(saveData, player, false)
		end
	end
end)

-- Save everyone when the server shuts down
game:BindToClose(function()
	local remaining = 0
	for player in pairs(profiles) do
		remaining += 1
		task.spawn(function()
			saveData(player, true)
			remaining -= 1
		end)
	end
	local start = os.clock()
	while remaining > 0 and os.clock() - start < 25 do
		task.wait()
	end
end)

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- PUBLIC API
---------------------------------------------------------------------
function DataManager.Get(player)
	return profiles[player]
end

function DataManager.WaitForData(player, timeout)
	local start = os.clock()
	while not profiles[player] and player.Parent do
		if timeout and os.clock() - start > timeout then return nil end
		task.wait()
	end
	return profiles[player]
end

-- Coins ---------------------------------------------------------------
function DataManager.AddCoins(player, amount)
	local data = profiles[player]
	if not data or amount <= 0 then return end
	data.Coins += math.floor(amount)
	syncAttributes(player, data)
end

function DataManager.SpendCoins(player, amount)
	local data = profiles[player]
	if not data or amount < 0 or data.Coins < amount then
		return false
	end
	data.Coins -= math.floor(amount)
	syncAttributes(player, data)
	return true
end

-- Slots ---------------------------------------------------------------
function DataManager.GetMaxSlots(player)
	local data = profiles[player]
	if not data then return BASE_SLOTS end
	local slots = BASE_SLOTS + math.min(data.Rebirths, MAX_REBIRTH_SLOTS)
	if player:GetAttribute("HasExtraSlotPass") then
		slots += 1
	end
	return slots
end

function DataManager.CountBlobs(player)
	local data = profiles[player]
	if not data then return 0 end
	local count = 0
	for _ in pairs(data.Blobs) do count += 1 end
	return count
end

-- Blobs ---------------------------------------------------------------
function DataManager.AddBlob(player, blobType)
	local data = profiles[player]
	if not data then return nil, "Data not loaded" end
	if not BlobDefinitions.Exists(blobType) then return nil, "Unknown blob type" end
	if DataManager.CountBlobs(player) >= DataManager.GetMaxSlots(player) then
		return nil, "No free pet slots"
	end

	local allocated, bonus = {}, {}
	for _, stat in ipairs(BlobDefinitions.StatOrder) do
		allocated[stat] = 0
		bonus[stat] = 0
	end

	local id = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false)
	local blob = {
		Id = id,
		Type = blobType,
		Nickname = "",
		Level = 1,
		XP = 0,
		UnspentPoints = 0,
		Allocated = allocated, -- points the player chose
		Bonus = bonus,         -- points from rare bugs etc.
		Ability = "",          -- special ability name; "" = none bought yet
		Cosmetics = {},        -- [slot] = itemName, e.g. Hat = "TopHat"
		HatchedAt = os.time(),
	}

	data.Blobs[id] = blob
	data.Progress.TotalHatched += 1
	if data.EquippedBlobId == "" then
		data.EquippedBlobId = id
	end
	syncAttributes(player, data)
	return blob
end

function DataManager.GetBlob(player, blobId)
	local data = profiles[player]
	return data and data.Blobs[blobId]
end

-- Adds XP and handles level-ups. Returns how many levels were gained.
function DataManager.AddXP(player, blobId, amount)
	local blob = DataManager.GetBlob(player, blobId)
	if not blob or amount <= 0 then return 0 end

	blob.XP += amount
	local gained = 0
	while blob.Level < BlobDefinitions.MaxLevel
		and blob.XP >= BlobDefinitions.XPToNextLevel(blob.Level) do
		blob.XP -= BlobDefinitions.XPToNextLevel(blob.Level)
		blob.Level += 1
		blob.UnspentPoints += BlobDefinitions.PointsPerLevel
		gained += 1
	end
	return gained
end

function DataManager.SpendStatPoint(player, blobId, statName)
	local blob = DataManager.GetBlob(player, blobId)
	if not blob then return false end
	if blob.UnspentPoints <= 0 then return false end
	if blob.Allocated[statName] == nil then return false end

	blob.UnspentPoints -= 1
	blob.Allocated[statName] += 1
	return true
end

return DataManager

--[[
	PlayerSetup (Script)
	Put this in ServerScriptService, next to the DataManager module.

	• Creates the leaderboard (Coins, Rebirths) once a player's data loads
	• Keeps the leaderboard in sync when coins change
	• TEST MODE (Studio only): gives 100 coins each time you join and hatches
	  a free test blob, then prints your save so you can see it persist.
]]

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local DataManager = require(ServerScriptService:WaitForChild("DataManager"))
local BlobDefinitions = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BlobDefinitions"))

local TEST_MODE = true -- set to false before you publish the real game

local function createLeaderstats(player, data)
	local leaderstats = Instance.new("Folder")
	leaderstats.Name = "leaderstats"

	local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
	coins.Name = "Coins"
	coins.Value = data.Coins
	coins.Parent = leaderstats

	local rebirths = Instance.new("IntValue")
	rebirths.Name = "Rebirths"
	rebirths.Value = data.Rebirths
	rebirths.Parent = leaderstats

	leaderstats.Parent = player

	-- DataManager updates these attributes whenever values change
	player:GetAttributeChangedSignal("Coins"):Connect(function()
		coins.Value = player:GetAttribute("Coins") or 0
	end)
	player:GetAttributeChangedSignal("Rebirths"):Connect(function()
		rebirths.Value = player:GetAttribute("Rebirths") or 0
	end)
end

local function printSave(player, data)
	print(("===== %s's save ====="):format(player.Name))
	print("Coins:", data.Coins, "| Rebirths:", data.Rebirths,
		"| Slots:", DataManager.CountBlobs(player) .. "/" .. DataManager.GetMaxSlots(player))
	for id, blob in pairs(data.Blobs) do
		local stats = BlobDefinitions.GetAllStats(blob)
		print(("  %s (Lv %d, %d XP, %d unspent points) id=%s"):format(
			blob.Type, blob.Level, blob.XP, blob.UnspentPoints, id))
		print(("    HP %d | STA %d | MEL %d | RNG %d | SPD %.1f | AP %d"):format(
			stats.Health, stats.Stamina, stats.Melee, stats.Range, stats.Speed, stats.AbilityPower))
	end
end

local function runTest(player, data)
	DataManager.AddCoins(player, 100)

	-- Hatch one test blob if they have none
	if DataManager.CountBlobs(player) == 0 then
		local blob, reason = DataManager.AddBlob(player, "Bouncer")
		if blob then
			print("[Test] Hatched a test Bouncer")
		else
			warn("[Test] Couldn't hatch:", reason)
		end
	end

	-- Give the equipped blob some XP and spend a point, to test leveling
	local blobId = data.EquippedBlobId
	if blobId ~= "" then
		local levels = DataManager.AddXP(player, blobId, 120)
		if levels > 0 then
			print(("[Test] Blob gained %d level(s)"):format(levels))
		end
		DataManager.SpendStatPoint(player, blobId, "Speed")
	end

	printSave(player, data)
end

local function onLoaded(player, data)
	createLeaderstats(player, data)

	if TEST_MODE and RunService:IsStudio() then
		runTest(player, data)
	end
end

DataManager.Loaded:Connect(onLoaded)

-- In case anyone finished loading before this script connected

--[[
	BlobDefinitions (ModuleScript)
	Put this in ReplicatedStorage so both the server and players' UI can read it.

	This is the ONE place that describes every blob type in the game.
	To add a new blob later, copy one entry in Blobs, give it a new key,
	and change its numbers. Everything else in the game reads from here.

	MODELS: each blob's model goes in ReplicatedStorage > BlobModels,
	and the model's name must match that blob's ModelName below exactly.
]]

local BlobDefinitions = {}

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STATS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The order here is the order they show up in the stat screen.
BlobDefinitions.StatOrder = { "Health", "Stamina", "Melee", "Range", "Speed", "AbilityPower" }

-- How much ONE stat point adds to each stat
BlobDefinitions.StatPerPoint = {
	Health       = 10,
	Stamina      = 5,
	Melee        = 2,
	Range        = 2,
	Speed        = 0.5,
	AbilityPower = 3,
}

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- RARITIES
---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Only Common blobs exist right now; the others are ready for later.
BlobDefinitions.Rarities = {
	Common    = { Order = 1, Color = Color3.fromRGB(190, 190, 190) },
	Uncommon  = { Order = 2, Color = Color3.fromRGB(85, 200, 90) },
	Rare      = { Order = 3, Color = Color3.fromRGB(70, 140, 255) },
	Epic      = { Order = 4, Color = Color3.fromRGB(170, 85, 255) },
	Legendary = { Order = 5, Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 180, 40) },
}

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- ELEMENTS (for battles later, e.g. Water beats Fire)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
BlobDefinitions.Elements = { "Nature", "Water", "Electric", "Fire", "Mystic", "Stone" }

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- GROWTH & LEVELING
---------------------------------------------------------------------
BlobDefinitions.HatchSize       = 0.4 -- blobs hatch at 40% of full size
BlobDefinitions.PointsPerLevel  = 1   -- stat points gained each level
BlobDefinitions.MaxLevel        = 100

-- XP needed to go from `level` to `level + 1`
function BlobDefinitions.XPToNextLevel(level)
	return math.floor(50 * level ^ 1.5)
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- BLOB TYPES  (your 6 starter blobs, left to right in your screenshot)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
--[[
	Each entry, explained:

	DisplayName     : name players see in menus (can have spaces)
	Description     : one line shown in the egg / pet menu
	Rarity          : one of the Rarities above
	Element         : one of the Elements above
	MovementStyle   : how it moves on the plot (Bounce, Roll, Hop, Wobble, Slither, Hover)
	FullSize        : height in studs when fully grown
	FullGrowthLevel : level where it reaches full size; after this only stats grow
	BaseStats       : starting stats before any points are spent
	ModelName       : EXACT name of its model in ReplicatedStorage > BlobModels

	Names are placeholders — rename anything you like. If you rename the
	key (e.g. Sprout = {), also rename it anywhere else it's used.
]]
BlobDefinitions.Blobs = {
	-- 1. Green blob with ferns
	Sprout = {
		DisplayName = "Sprout",
		Description = "A leafy little blob that heals in the sunshine.",
		Rarity = "Common",
		Element = "Nature",
		MovementStyle = "Hop",
		FullSize = 6,
		FullGrowthLevel = 20,
		BaseStats = { Health = 120, Stamina = 55, Melee = 9, Range = 9, Speed = 15, AbilityPower = 12 },
		ModelName = "Sprout",
	},

	-- 2. Blue water blob with coral
	Coral = {
		DisplayName = "Coral",
		Description = "Splashes enemies from a distance with bubbles.",
		Rarity = "Common",
		Element = "Water",
		MovementStyle = "Roll",
		FullSize = 6,
		FullGrowthLevel = 20,
		BaseStats = { Health = 100, Stamina = 55, Melee = 8, Range = 13, Speed = 16, AbilityPower = 10 },
		ModelName = "Coral",
	},

	-- 3. Yellow angry blob with lightning
	Zap = {
		DisplayName = "Zap",
		Description = "Crackling with energy and always in a bad mood.",
		Rarity = "Common",
		Element = "Electric",
		MovementStyle = "Bounce",
		FullSize = 5.5,
		FullGrowthLevel = 20,
		BaseStats = { Health = 85, Stamina = 60, Melee = 11, Range = 10, Speed = 19, AbilityPower = 10 },
		ModelName = "Zap",
	},

	-- 4. Orange fire blob
	Ember = {
		DisplayName = "Ember",
		Description = "A hot-headed blob that loves to charge in.",
		Rarity = "Common",
		Element = "Fire",
		MovementStyle = "Bounce",
		FullSize = 6,
		FullGrowthLevel = 20,
		BaseStats = { Health = 95, Stamina = 50, Melee = 14, Range = 8, Speed = 17, AbilityPower = 10 },
		ModelName = "Ember",
	},

	-- 5. Blue drop-shaped blob with one big eye
	Gazer = {
		DisplayName = "Gazer",
		Description = "Sees everything. Its stare hits from far away.",
		Rarity = "Common",
		Element = "Mystic",
		MovementStyle = "Slither",
		FullSize = 6.5,
		FullGrowthLevel = 20,
		BaseStats = { Health = 90, Stamina = 55, Melee = 7, Range = 14, Speed = 15, AbilityPower = 13 },
		ModelName = "Gazer",
	},

	-- 6. Pale blue carved stone-face blob
	Stoneface = {
		DisplayName = "Stoneface",
		Description = "Ancient, slow and nearly impossible to knock down.",
		Rarity = "Common",
		Element = "Stone",
		MovementStyle = "Wobble",
		FullSize = 7,
		FullGrowthLevel = 20,
		BaseStats = { Health = 140, Stamina = 45, Melee = 12, Range = 6, Speed = 13, AbilityPower = 10 },
		ModelName = "Stoneface",
	},
}

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- HELPERS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
function BlobDefinitions.Get(blobType)
	return BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobType]
end

function BlobDefinitions.Exists(blobType)
	return BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobType] ~= nil
end

-- Size multiplier (0.4 → 1.0) for a blob at a given level
function BlobDefinitions.GetSizeScale(blobType, level)
	local def = BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobType]
	if not def then return 1 end
	local progress = math.clamp((level - 1) / (def.FullGrowthLevel - 1), 0, 1)
	return BlobDefinitions.HatchSize + (1 - BlobDefinitions.HatchSize) * progress
end

-- Finds this blob type's model in ReplicatedStorage > BlobModels (nil if missing)
function BlobDefinitions.GetModel(blobType)
	local def = BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobType]
	if not def then return nil end
	local folder = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):FindFirstChild("BlobModels")
	return folder and folder:FindFirstChild(def.ModelName)
end

-- Final value of one stat for a saved blob: base + spent points + bug bonuses
function BlobDefinitions.GetStat(blobData, statName)
	local def = BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobData.Type]
	if not def then return 0 end
	local base = def.BaseStats[statName] or 0
	local spent = (blobData.Allocated and blobData.Allocated[statName]) or 0
	local bonus = (blobData.Bonus and blobData.Bonus[statName]) or 0
	return base + (spent + bonus) * (BlobDefinitions.StatPerPoint[statName] or 0)
end

-- All final stats at once, as a table
function BlobDefinitions.GetAllStats(blobData)
	local result = {}
	for _, statName in ipairs(BlobDefinitions.StatOrder) do
		result[statName] = BlobDefinitions.GetStat(blobData, statName)
	end
	return result
end

return BlobDefinitions

**In ReplicatedStorage:**

1. **Rename `Blobmodels` to `BlobModels`** (capital M). Click it, then edit **Name** in Properties.
2. **Move the ModuleScript out of the folder.** Drag `ModuleScript` onto **ReplicatedStorage** so it sits next to BlobModels, not inside it. Then rename it to `BlobDefinitions`. Open it and make sure the BlobDefinitions code is pasted inside.

-- All final stats at once, as a table
function BlobDefinitions.GetAllStats(blobData)
	local result = {}
	for _, statName in ipairs(BlobDefinitions.StatOrder) do
		result[statName] = BlobDefinitions.GetStat(blobData, statName)
	end
	return result
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- EGGS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
--[[
	Weights decide the chance of each blob. A blob's chance is its weight
	divided by the total of all weights in that egg.

	Example: Sprout = 30, Coral = 10 → Sprout 75%, Coral 25%.
	Right now every blob has the same weight, so each is a 1-in-6 chance.

	Later eggs that cost coins or Robux must show these odds to players
	before they buy (GetEggOdds below gives you the percentages).
]]
BlobDefinitions.Eggs = {
	Starter = {
		DisplayName = "Starter Egg",
		Price = 0,
		Weights = {
			Sprout = 1,
			Coral = 1,
			Zap = 1,
			Ember = 1,
			Gazer = 1,
			Stoneface = 1,
		},
	},
}

-- Returns { blobType = percent } for an egg, e.g. { Sprout = 16.7, ... }
function BlobDefinitions.GetEggOdds(eggName)
	local egg = BlobDefinitions.Eggs[eggName]
	if not egg then return {} end
	local total = 0
	for _, weight in pairs(egg.Weights) do
		total += weight
	end
	local odds = {}
	for blobType, weight in pairs(egg.Weights) do
		odds[blobType] = math.floor(weight / total * 1000 + 0.5) / 10
	end
	return odds
end

local rng = Random.new()

-- Picks a random blob type from an egg using its weights
function BlobDefinitions.RollEgg(eggName)
	local egg = BlobDefinitions.Eggs[eggName]
	if not egg then return nil end

	local total = 0
	for blobType, weight in pairs(egg.Weights) do
		if BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobType] then
			total += weight
		end
	end

	local roll = rng:NextNumber(0, total)
	local last
	for blobType, weight in pairs(egg.Weights) do
		if BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobType] then
			last = blobType
			roll -= weight
			if roll <= 0 then
				return blobType
			end
		end
	end
	return last
end

--[[
	StarterEgg (Script)
	Put this in ServerScriptService.

	Gives every brand-new player ONE free Starter Egg:
	  1. When their save loads, checks if they've already had their starter egg
	  2. If not, rolls a random blob from the Starter egg's odds
	  3. Adds the blob to their save, marks the egg as received, and saves
	  4. Tells their game to play the hatching animation

	Because "ReceivedStarterEgg" is saved, rejoining never gives another egg.
	The blob is saved BEFORE the animation plays, so leaving mid-animation
	can't lose it.
]]

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local DataManager = require(ServerScriptService:WaitForChild("DataManager"))
local BlobDefinitions = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BlobDefinitions"))

local STARTER_EGG = "Starter"
local DELAY_AFTER_SPAWN = 2 -- seconds to wait after spawning on the plot

-- RemoteEvent the server uses to tell a player "play the hatch animation"
local remotes = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("Remotes")
if not remotes then
	remotes = Instance.new("Folder")
	remotes.Name = "Remotes"
	remotes.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
end

local playHatch = remotes:FindFirstChild("PlayHatch")
if not playHatch then
	playHatch = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
	playHatch.Name = "PlayHatch"
	playHatch.Parent = remotes
end

local function giveStarterEgg(player, data)
	if data.Progress.ReceivedStarterEgg then
		return -- already had it
	end

	-- Older saves that already own blobs with no free slot: just mark it done
	if DataManager.CountBlobs(player) >= DataManager.GetMaxSlots(player) then
		data.Progress.ReceivedStarterEgg = true
		return
	end

	local blobType = BlobDefinitions.RollEgg(STARTER_EGG)
	local blob, reason = DataManager.AddBlob(player, blobType)
	if not blob then
		warn(("[StarterEgg] Couldn't give %s a starter blob: %s"):format(player.Name, tostring(reason)))
		return
	end

	data.Progress.ReceivedStarterEgg = true
	print(("[StarterEgg] %s hatched a %s"):format(player.Name, blobType))
	task.spawn(DataManager.Save, player)

	-- Wait until they've spawned on their plot, then play the animation
	local character = player.Character or player.CharacterAdded:Wait()
	character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart", 10)
	task.wait(DELAY_AFTER_SPAWN)

	if player.Parent then
		playHatch:FireClient(player, blobType, STARTER_EGG)
	end
end

DataManager.Loaded:Connect(giveStarterEgg)

-- In case anyone finished loading before this script connected
for _, player in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
	local data = DataManager.Get(player)
	if data then
		task.spawn(giveStarterEgg, player, data)
	end
end

--[[
	HatchAnimation (LocalScript)
	Put this in StarterPlayer > StarterPlayerScripts.

	Plays when the server says "this player hatched a blob":
	  1. An egg drops onto the ground in front of the player
	  2. The camera swings around to look at it
	  3. The egg wobbles three times, harder each time, then shakes
	  4. White flash + sparkles, and the baby blob pops out
	  5. A card shows the blob's name, rarity and element
	  6. Click "Awesome!" (or wait) and everything goes back to normal

	Everything here is only visible to this player.
]]

local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local BlobDefinitions = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BlobDefinitions"))
local playHatch = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Remotes"):WaitForChild("PlayHatch")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SETTINGS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local EGG_DISTANCE   = 10                          -- studs in front of the player
local EGG_SIZE       = Vector3.new(3, 4, 3)
local EGG_COLOR      = Color3.fromRGB(255, 244, 214)
local SPOT_COLOR     = Color3.fromRGB(120, 200, 140)
local CAMERA_BACK    = 11                          -- camera distance from the egg
local CAMERA_UP      = 3.5
local AUTO_CLOSE     = 12                          -- seconds before the card closes itself

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- HELPERS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Runs step(alpha) every frame, alpha going 0 → 1 over `duration` seconds
local function animate(duration, step)
	local start = os.clock()
	while true do
		local alpha = math.min((os.clock() - start) / duration, 1)
		step(alpha)
		if alpha >= 1 then break end
		RunService.RenderStepped:Wait()
	end
end

local function easeOutBack(a)
	local c1 = 1.70158
	local c3 = c1 + 1
	return 1 + c3 * (a - 1) ^ 3 + c1 * (a - 1) ^ 2
end

local function easeOutBounce(a)
	if a < 1 / 2.75 then
		return 7.5625 * a * a
	elseif a < 2 / 2.75 then
		a -= 1.5 / 2.75
		return 7.5625 * a * a + 0.75
	elseif a < 2.5 / 2.75 then
		a -= 2.25 / 2.75
		return 7.5625 * a * a + 0.9375
	else
		a -= 2.625 / 2.75
		return 7.5625 * a * a + 0.984375
	end
end

-- Finds the ground below a point (ignoring the player's own character)
local function groundBelow(position, character)
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { character }
	local result = workspace:Raycast(position + Vector3.new(0, 10, 0), Vector3.new(0, -60, 0), params)
	return result and result.Position or (position - Vector3.new(0, 3, 0))
end

local function new(className, props, children)
	local inst = Instance.new(className)
	for key, value in pairs(props or {}) do
		inst[key] = value
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(children or {}) do
		child.Parent = inst
	end
	return inst
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- THE EGG
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function buildEgg()
	local egg = Instance.new("Model")
	egg.Name = "HatchEgg"

	local body = new("Part", {
		Name = "Body",
		Size = EGG_SIZE,
		Color = EGG_COLOR,
		Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic,
		Anchored = true,
		CanCollide = false,
		CastShadow = true,
	}, {
		new("SpecialMesh", { MeshType = Enum.MeshType.Sphere }),
	})
	body.Parent = egg
	egg.PrimaryPart = body

	-- Spots spread around the shell
	local rx, ry, rz = EGG_SIZE.X / 2, EGG_SIZE.Y / 2, EGG_SIZE.Z / 2
	local spots = {
		{ 0.4, 0.0 }, { -0.1, 1.3 }, { 0.6, 2.6 }, { -0.3, 3.7 }, { 0.2, 5.0 }, { 0.9, 1.0 },
	}
	for _, spot in ipairs(spots) do
		local lat, lon = spot[1], spot[2]
		local offset = Vector3.new(
			rx * math.cos(lat) * math.cos(lon),
			ry * math.sin(lat),
			rz * math.cos(lat) * math.sin(lon)
		) * 0.93
		local part = new("Part", {
			Name = "Spot",
			Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball,
			Size = Vector3.new(0.8, 0.8, 0.8),
			Color = SPOT_COLOR,
			Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic,
			Anchored = true,
			CanCollide = false,
			CFrame = CFrame.new(offset),
		})
		part.Parent = egg
	end

	return egg
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- THE BABY BLOB
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function buildBlob(blobType)
	local def = BlobDefinitions.Get(blobType)
	local template = BlobDefinitions.GetModel(blobType)
	local model

	if template and template:IsA("Model") then
		model = template:Clone()
		-- Anything inside the model that runs code shouldn't run in the animation
		for _, d in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
			if d:IsA("BaseScript") then d:Destroy() end
		end
	else
		-- No model found: use a placeholder ball so the animation still works
		warn("[HatchAnimation] No model for " .. tostring(blobType) .. " in ReplicatedStorage.BlobModels")
		model = Instance.new("Model")
		local ball = new("Part", {
			Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball,
			Size = Vector3.new(4, 4, 4),
			Color = def and BlobDefinitions.Rarities[def.Rarity].Color or Color3.new(1, 1, 1),
		})
		ball.Parent = model
		model.PrimaryPart = ball
	end

	for _, d in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
		if d:IsA("BasePart") then
			d.Anchored = true
			d.CanCollide = false
		end
	end

	-- Scale to baby size: full height × hatch size (40%)
	local _, size = model:GetBoundingBox()
	local fullSize = def and def.FullSize or 6
	local targetHeight = fullSize * BlobDefinitions.HatchSize
	local babyScale = model:GetScale() * (targetHeight / math.max(size.Y, 0.1))

	return model, babyScale
end

-- Puts a model so it sits on the ground at `groundPos`, facing `lookAt`
local function placeOnGround(model, groundPos, lookAt)
	local facing = CFrame.lookAt(groundPos, Vector3.new(lookAt.X, groundPos.Y, lookAt.Z))
	model:PivotTo(facing)
	local boxCFrame, boxSize = model:GetBoundingBox()
	local bottom = boxCFrame.Position.Y - boxSize.Y / 2
	local placed = facing + Vector3.new(0, groundPos.Y - bottom, 0)
	model:PivotTo(placed)
	return placed
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- THE REVEAL CARD
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function buildCard(blobType)
	local def = BlobDefinitions.Get(blobType)
	local rarity = def and def.Rarity or "Common"
	local rarityColor = BlobDefinitions.Rarities[rarity].Color

	local gui = new("ScreenGui", {
		Name = "HatchCard",
		ResetOnSpawn = false,
		IgnoreGuiInset = true,
		DisplayOrder = 50,
	})

	local card = new("Frame", {
		Name = "Card",
		AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 1),
		Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.4, 0), -- starts off-screen, slides up
		Size = UDim2.new(0, 360, 0, 190),
		BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(28, 30, 38),
		BackgroundTransparency = 0.05,
	}, {
		new("UICorner", { CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, 16) }),
		new("UIStroke", { Color = rarityColor, Thickness = 3 }),
		new("TextLabel", {
			Name = "Heading",
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 14),
			Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 22),
			Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold,
			Text = "You hatched...",
			TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(200, 205, 220),
			TextSize = 18,
		}),
		new("TextLabel", {
			Name = "BlobName",
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 38),
			Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 46),
			Font = Enum.Font.FredokaOne,
			Text = def and def.DisplayName or blobType,
			TextColor3 = rarityColor,
			TextSize = 42,
		}),
		new("TextLabel", {
			Name = "Details",
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 86),
			Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 20),
			Font = Enum.Font.GothamMedium,
			Text = rarity .. "  •  " .. (def and def.Element or "?"),
			TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(230, 230, 240),
			TextSize = 16,
		}),
		new("TextLabel", {
			Name = "Description",
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Position = UDim2.new(0, 20, 0, 108),
			Size = UDim2.new(1, -40, 0, 20),
			Font = Enum.Font.Gotham,
			Text = def and def.Description or "",
			TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(170, 175, 190),
			TextSize = 14,
			TextWrapped = true,
		}),
	})
	card.Parent = gui

	local button = new("TextButton", {
		Name = "Close",
		AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 1),
		Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1, -14),
		Size = UDim2.new(0, 170, 0, 40),
		BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(88, 196, 108),
		Font = Enum.Font.FredokaOne,
		Text = "Awesome!",
		TextColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1),
		TextSize = 22,
		AutoButtonColor = true,
	}, {
		new("UICorner", { CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, 12) }),
	})
	button.Parent = card

	local flash = new("Frame", {
		Name = "Flash",
		Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1),
		BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1),
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		ZIndex = 10,
	})
	flash.Parent = gui

	return gui, card, button, flash
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- MAIN SEQUENCE
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local busy = false

local function playHatchSequence(blobType)
	while busy do task.wait(0.2) end
	busy = true

	local character = player.Character or player.CharacterAdded:Wait()
	local root = character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart", 10)
	local humanoid = character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not root or not humanoid then
		busy = false
		return
	end

	-- Freeze the player during the animation
	local oldWalk, oldJumpPower, oldJumpHeight = humanoid.WalkSpeed, humanoid.JumpPower, humanoid.JumpHeight
	humanoid.WalkSpeed, humanoid.JumpPower, humanoid.JumpHeight = 0, 0, 0
	humanoid:Move(Vector3.zero)

	-- Where the egg lands: in front of the player, on the ground
	local flatLook = Vector3.new(root.CFrame.LookVector.X, 0, root.CFrame.LookVector.Z)
	if flatLook.Magnitude < 0.01 then flatLook = Vector3.new(0, 0, -1) end
	flatLook = flatLook.Unit
	local ground = groundBelow(root.Position + flatLook * EGG_DISTANCE, character)
	local eggCenter = ground + Vector3.new(0, EGG_SIZE.Y / 2, 0)

	-- Camera sits between the player and the egg, looking at the egg
	local camPos = eggCenter - flatLook * CAMERA_BACK + Vector3.new(0, CAMERA_UP, 0)
	local camTarget = CFrame.lookAt(camPos, eggCenter)
	camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable
	TweenService:Create(camera, TweenInfo.new(0.8, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
		{ CFrame = camTarget }):Play()

	-- 1. Egg drops from the sky and bounces
	local egg = buildEgg()
	local eggBase = CFrame.lookAt(eggCenter, Vector3.new(camPos.X, eggCenter.Y, camPos.Z))
	local dropHeight = 18
	egg:PivotTo(eggBase + Vector3.new(0, dropHeight, 0))
	egg.Parent = workspace
	animate(0.9, function(a)
		egg:PivotTo(eggBase + Vector3.new(0, dropHeight * (1 - easeOutBounce(a)), 0))
	end)
	task.wait(0.4)

	-- 2. Wobble three times, harder each time
	for i, strength in ipairs({ 10, 18, 28 }) do
		local maxAngle = math.rad(strength)
		animate(0.55, function(a)
			local angle = math.sin(a * math.pi * 4) * maxAngle * (1 - a)
			egg:PivotTo(eggBase * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, angle))
		end)
		task.wait(i < 3 and 0.45 or 0.2)
	end

	-- 3. Rapid shake while swelling up
	local eggScale = egg:GetScale()
	animate(0.7, function(a)
		local shake = math.rad(12) * (0.4 + a)
		egg:ScaleTo(eggScale * (1 + 0.25 * a))
		egg:PivotTo(eggBase * CFrame.Angles(
			(math.random() - 0.5) * shake, 0, (math.random() - 0.5) * shake))
	end)

	-- 4. Flash, sparkles, egg disappears
	local gui, card, button, flash = buildCard(blobType)
	gui.Parent = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")
	flash.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	TweenService:Create(flash, TweenInfo.new(0.7), { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }):Play()

	local burst = new("Part", {
		Anchored = true, CanCollide = false, Transparency = 1,
		Size = Vector3.new(1, 1, 1), CFrame = CFrame.new(eggCenter),
	})
	local sparkles = new("ParticleEmitter", {
		Texture = "rbxasset://textures/particles/sparkles_main.dds",
		Speed = NumberRange.new(10, 18),
		SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(180, 180),
		Lifetime = NumberRange.new(0.6, 1.2),
		Size = NumberSequence.new({ NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 1.2), NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0) }),
		Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromRGB(255, 240, 180)),
		LightEmission = 1,
		Rate = 0,
	})
	sparkles.Parent = burst
	burst.Parent = workspace
	sparkles:Emit(60)
	Debris:AddItem(burst, 3)
	egg:Destroy()

	-- 5. Baby blob pops out
	local blob, babyScale = buildBlob(blobType)
	blob:ScaleTo(babyScale)
	blob.Parent = workspace
	local restCFrame = placeOnGround(blob, ground, camPos)

	animate(0.45, function(a)
		blob:ScaleTo(babyScale * math.max(0.05, easeOutBack(a)))
		placeOnGround(blob, ground, camPos)
	end)
	blob:ScaleTo(babyScale)
	restCFrame = placeOnGround(blob, ground, camPos)

	-- Gentle happy sway + little hops while the card is up
	local start = os.clock()
	local idle = RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function()
		local t = os.clock() - start
		local hop = math.abs(math.sin(t * 3)) * 0.5
		local sway = math.sin(t * 1.6) * math.rad(20)
		blob:PivotTo(restCFrame * CFrame.Angles(0, sway, 0) + Vector3.new(0, hop, 0))
	end)

	-- 6. Slide the card up and wait for "Awesome!" (or the timeout)
	TweenService:Create(card, TweenInfo.new(0.5, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
		{ Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1, -30) }):Play()

	local closed = false
	button.Activated:Connect(function() closed = true end)
	local waitStart = os.clock()
	while not closed and os.clock() - waitStart < AUTO_CLOSE do
		task.wait(0.1)
	end

	-- 7. Clean up and give control back
	idle:Disconnect()
	local slideOut = TweenService:Create(card, TweenInfo.new(0.3), { Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.4, 0) })
	slideOut:Play()
	slideOut.Completed:Wait()
	gui:Destroy()
	blob:Destroy()

	camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Custom
	camera.CameraSubject = humanoid
	if humanoid.Parent then
		humanoid.WalkSpeed, humanoid.JumpPower, humanoid.JumpHeight = oldWalk, oldJumpPower, oldJumpHeight
	end

	busy = false
end

playHatch.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(blobType)
	task.spawn(playHatchSequence, blobType)
end)

# Imagine — Visual Creation Suite ## Modules Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance: - `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams - `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards - `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls - `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth) - `art` — illustration and generative art Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance. **Complexity budget — hard limits:** - Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box. - Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp. - Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams. If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything. **Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `

` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.) You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat. ## Core Design System These rules apply to ALL use cases. ### Philosophy - **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins. - **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces. - **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text. - **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. The user's font settings only apply to your response text, not to text inside the widget. ### Streaming Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early. - **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last. - **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately. - Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream. - Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS. - Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead. ### Rules - No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming) - No font-size below 11px - No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths. - No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects - No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg) - **Typography**: The default font is Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-voice)`. - **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI. - **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings. - **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only. - The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element. - Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style="min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;">` and put the modal inside — it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height. - **Fullscreen / expand buttons**: there is no fullscreen. Never call any element's `requestFullscreen()`, never call `document.exitFullscreen()`, and never key state on `document.fullscreenElement` (the API is dead inside the widget iframe and `fullscreenElement` stays null forever, so a label or branch keyed on it is permanently stuck), never call display-mode host APIs, and never fake fullscreen by restyling your container to viewport size — all of these produce dead or broken controls on at least one platform. If the user asks for a fullscreen or expand button, implement an expanded-layout toggle instead: a synchronous CSS class flip on in-flow content with explicit px sizes (taller chart, roomier controls), updating the button label in the same handler — no async, no awaits, symmetric enter/exit. Tokens tell you _what_ you can use; the [Rules](../CLAUDE.md#rules) tell you _how_ to apply them. These principles tell you _why_. ## Claude-native cds is designed to be authored _by_ Claude as much as _for_ Claude's products. The `CLAUDE.md` you're reading is the system prompt; component docs are structured for retrieval; utilities are named so a model can guess them; the GenerateDemo page proves the loop works. A design system an LLM can use fluently is one humans can use fluently too. ## Clay is Claude's color `brand` (clay) is reserved for what Claude does — send, generate, the spark mark. User-driven primary actions take the neutral `accent` blue; everything else stays gray. Holding clay back to a single role is what lets it carry meaning instead of becoming wallpaper. ## Serif is Claude's voice Claude's responses render in serif; the surrounding chrome stays sans. Typography signals who's speaking before a word is read. cds ships `--font-voice` (the `font-voice` utility) for response surfaces. ## Density adapts to the surface Console, claude.ai and antfarm share the same components — `compact` for dev tools and power users, `comfortable` for consumer apps. Density is one switch on `CdsRoot`, not a per-component prop, so a product can change its feel without forking a single component. ## Built to be composed, not overridden Every component takes `className` for placement and behavior, every token is a public CSS var, and compound parts (`.Root`, `.Item`, `.Trigger`) sit under the porcelain helpers so you can recombine them. The system expects you to compose _with_ it — wrap it, arrange it, fill its slots, build new things from its tokens — not restyle it from outside or fork it. When props and parts can't reach what you need, the system is missing something: the fix goes into cds (see the [`className` rule](../CLAUDE.md#classname-rule)), not around it. ## Restraint over options One accent per view, one elevation step, t-shirt sizes instead of 0–12 scales. Fewer decisions at the call site means fewer ways for two screens to drift apart — consistency comes from removing knobs, not policing them. ## CDS tokens Every visual decision in `@ant/cds` resolves to a `--*` CSS custom property. Text on it keeps its own color and weight. #### Palette tints `--bg-tint-{hue}` for the eight chromatic hues (`red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `aqua`, `blue`, `violet`, `magenta`; utility `bg-tint-{hue}`) is the translucent chip tint: a 35%-alpha tint in light (75% in dark) whose channels are solved against `surface-1` so that on a plain surface it composites to the same opaque hue-100 (hue-800 in dark) stop `bg-{role}` paints while a hover or selected wash underneath still shows through. `Badge` uses it for every tinted variant (semantic and palette); `bg-{role}` stays the opaque tint for Banner, Toast and larger surfaces. Pair with `--text-tint-{hue}` (utility `text-tint-{hue}`; hue-600, 300 in dark) so bg and text follow the same CdsRoot's mode. `--bg-tint-{hue}-opaque` (utility `bg-tint-{hue}-opaque`) is that opaque stop as a token; a surface scope whose backdrop is a fill rather than a plane (CoachMark's accent card, `surface="fill-accent"`) re-points each `--bg-tint-{hue}` at it inline, because the un-mix only holds over a plane. The tints are solved against the stock `surface-1`, so a theme that overrides `--surface-*` should override `--bg-tint-*` in the same block if it needs the exact stops, and `--bg-tint-*-opaque` with them: inside a fill scope the inline pin reads the opaque token, not the tint. #### `git-*` roles Diff and PR/CR-state colors — `added`, `removed`, `modified`, `conflicting`, `merged`, `closed`, `draft`, plus `opened`/`queued` as aliases of `added`/`modified`. Each carries the full `text` / `fill{,-hover}` / `bg` / `border` / `on` suite. Values are hues matching the palette claude.ai's diff UI was built on (not CDS ramp stops), so adopting them there is a pure rename; `fill` light is the hue darkened just enough for white `on-git-*` to pass AA. ### Background vs. fill Both are backgrounds; the split is saturation, and therefore which foreground token pairs on top. `bg-{role}` is the pale tint (hue-100 light / hue-800 dark) for passive status surfaces — Banner, chip; Badge paints its translucent twin `bg-tint-{hue}`. Light enough that `text-{role}` (hue-600) reads against it: a danger banner is `bg-danger` + `text-danger`. `fill-{role}` is the saturated solid (hue-450) for interactive controls — button, checkbox, toggle. Too dark for `text-{role}`, so it pairs with `on-{role}` (gray-0 / gray-900) instead; the 450 stop is chosen for WCAG contrast against `on-*`. | | Background | Foreground | Example | | ----- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | | Tint | `bg-{role}` | `text-{role}` | Banner, Toast | | Solid | `fill-{role}` | `on-{role}` | Button | The token name encodes the pairing: use `bg-*` when the hue is ambient context behind body text; `fill-*` when the hue _is_ the control surface. ### Purpose tokens | Token | Value (light) | Use case | | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `--text-primary` | `neutral-900` | Body text | | `--text-secondary` | `neutral-600` | | | `--fill-field` | `hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.5)` (light) / `alpha-1` (dark) | Field control bg (TextInput, TextArea, Combobox) | | `--fill-field-ring` | `border` (light + dark) | Field control resting ring | | `--fill-ghost-hover` | `alpha-1` (light) / 7.5% white (dark half-step) | Ghost button / row hover bg | | `--fill-ghost-selected` | `alpha-2` (light) / 15% white (dark half-step) | Ghost row / nav item selected bg | | `--fill-control` | `alpha-2` | Avatar fallback bg | | `--fill-control-hover` | `alpha-3` | | | `--fill-disabled` | `alpha-1` | Disabled control bg | | `--on-primary` | `neutral-0` | Text on `fill-primary` | | `--on-accent` | `gray-0` | Text on `accent` | | `--on-brand` | `#ffffff` | Text on `brand` | | `--on-danger` | `gray-0` | Text on `danger` | | `--on-success` | `gray-900` ring | | `--shadow-sm` | two-layer via `--shadow-color` | Low elevation | | `--shadow-md` | two-layer via `--shadow-color` | Card / panel | | `--shadow-lg` | two-layer via `--shadow-color` | Dialog / sheet | | `--shadow-popover` | `0 8px 24px /12%, 0 2px 6px /8%` | Menu, dropdown popups | | `--surface-popover` | `surface-3` | Named alias | | `--surface-panel` | `surface-2` | Named alias | `--shadow-sm/md/lg` are two-layer composites (contact + diffused drop) driven by `--shadow-color`, which deepens to `black/24%` in dark mode. `--shadow-popover` is a fixed two-layer literal tuned for floating menus. --- ## CDS content How to write the words that go inside cds components. Tokens decide how the UI _looks_; this decides how it _sounds_. The voice is **intelligent, warm, unvarnished, and collaborative** — your smartest friend explaining something in plain terms. Friendly lives in the copy, not in extra chrome. ## Mechanics - **Sentence case everywhere.** Buttons, headings, tabs, labels, menu items. "Save changes", not "Save Changes". Title Case is for proper nouns only (Claude, Opus, Anthropic Console). - **No terminal punctuation on labels and headings.** Helper text, descriptions, and empty-state body copy _do_ end with a period. - **Use contractions.** "Can't", "you'll", "it's". Conversational, not stiff. - **Active voice, verb first.** "Delete project", not "Project deletion". - **Ellipsis = in progress only.** "Claude is thinking…". Not for trailing off, not for menu suffixes. - **No ampersands.** Spell out "and". - **Serial comma.** "Chats, projects, and artifacts." ## Pronouns UI speaks as the product, not as Claude and not as the user. | Context | Use | Example | | ---------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | | User's things | **your** | "Your projects" — never "My projects" | | Confirmations | none / past tense | "Saved", "Got it" — never "I saved it" | | Errors | **you / your** | "Your session expired" — never "I couldn't…" | | Claude (in chat) | **I** | Reserved for the chat surface; system UI never says "I" | ## Words to avoid | Skip | Why | Instead | | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------- | | "successfully" | The success toast _is_ the success | "File uploaded" | | "please" | UI isn't asking a favor | "Enter a name" | | "Click here" / "Tap to…" | Link text should name the destination | "Read the docs" | | "!" on system copy | Reads as shouty | "Settings saved" | | "leverage", "seamless", "unlock", "empower" | Corporate filler | Say what it does | | "simply", "just", "easy" | Presumes — and condescends | Cut it | ## Patterns **Buttons / CTAs** — verb first, 1–3 words, sentence case, no punctuation. "Create project", "Upgrade to Pro". Not "OK", "Submit", or "Click to continue". **Errors** — say what happened, then what to do. One sentence, no "Error:" prefix, no first person. "That name's already taken. Try another." Never surface raw exception strings. **Empty states** — an invitation, not an apology. Headline names the space ("Start your first project"), one-line body explains it, CTA is a verb ("Create project"). Skip "Nothing here yet." **Placeholders** — a real example of valid input ("name@company.com", "Summarize this document"). No "e.g." prefix, don't repeat the field label. **Links** — describe where they go ("Learn more", "View pricing"). Keep them at the end of the sentence; punctuation sits outside the link. ## Do / Don't | Do | Don't | | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | | "File uploaded" | "Your file was uploaded successfully!" | | "Enter a workspace name" | "Please enter a workspace name." | | "Couldn't connect to Slack. Retry" | "Error: I was unable to connect." | | "Your projects" | "My projects" | | "Create project" | "Click Here To Get Started" | | "Connect Slack" | "Add the Slack Connector" | Do not overthink. Try to keep thinking below 500 tokens. If the visual is complex and requires more reasoning effort, consider creating an artifact instead.

-- Blobs keep the upright pose they were built in, so they face the same
-- way they faced in Studio when you built them. Change this only if every
-- blob faces the wrong way in game (180 = turn all of them around).
BlobDefinitions.DefaultFacingOffset = 0

-- Extra turn (as a CFrame) that makes a blob's face point forward
function BlobDefinitions.GetFacingRotation(blobType)
	local def = BlobDefinitions.Blobs[blobType]
	local degrees = (def and def.FacingOffset) or BlobDefinitions.DefaultFacingOffset
	return CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(degrees), 0)
end

-- Lowest and highest points of a model in the world, ignoring how its
-- pivot is tilted (works for any model, however it was built)
function BlobDefinitions.GetWorldBounds(model)
	local bottom, top = math.huge, -math.huge
	for _, part in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
		if part:IsA("BasePart") then
			local cf, size = part.CFrame, part.Size
			local halfHeight = 0.5 * (math.abs(cf.RightVector.Y) * size.X
				+ math.abs(cf.UpVector.Y) * size.Y
				+ math.abs(cf.LookVector.Y) * size.Z)
			bottom = math.min(bottom, cf.Position.Y - halfHeight)
			top = math.max(top, cf.Position.Y + halfHeight)
		end
	end
	if bottom == math.huge then
		local pos = model:GetPivot().Position
		return pos.Y, pos.Y
	end
	return bottom, top
end

--[[
	BlobNaming (Script)
	Put this in ServerScriptService.

	Lets players give their blobs a name.
	  • The player's game sends (blobId, name) through Remotes > RenameBlob
	  • The server checks the blob really belongs to them
	  • The name is cleaned up and run through Roblox's text filter
	    (required by Roblox for anything other players can see)
	  • The filtered name is saved as the blob's Nickname

	An empty name clears the nickname, so the blob shows its type name again.
]]

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local TextService = game:GetService("TextService")

local DataManager = require(ServerScriptService:WaitForChild("DataManager"))
local BlobDefinitions = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BlobDefinitions"))

local COOLDOWN = 1 -- seconds between rename requests per player

local remotes = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("Remotes")
if not remotes then
	remotes = Instance.new("Folder")
	remotes.Name = "Remotes"
	remotes.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
end

local renameBlob = remotes:FindFirstChild("RenameBlob")
if not renameBlob then
	renameBlob = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
	renameBlob.Name = "RenameBlob"
	renameBlob.Parent = remotes
end

local lastRequest = {} -- [player] = time of last rename

-- Trims spaces, removes line breaks and limits the length
local function cleanName(text)
	text = text:gsub("[%c]", " ")          -- no new lines / control characters
	text = text:gsub("%s+", " ")           -- collapse repeated spaces
	text = text:match("^%s*(.-)%s*$") or "" -- trim the ends
	if utf8.len(text) and utf8.len(text) > BlobDefinitions.MaxNameLength then
		text = text:sub(1, utf8.offset(text, BlobDefinitions.MaxNameLength + 1) - 1)
	end
	return text
end

local function filterName(player, text)
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		local filtered = TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, player.UserId)
		return filtered:GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync()
	end)
	if ok then
		return result
	end
	warn("[BlobNaming] Filter failed for " .. player.Name .. ": " .. tostring(result))
	return nil
end

renameBlob.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, blobId, name)
	-- Never trust what a player's game sends: check everything
	if typeof(blobId) ~= "string" or typeof(name) ~= "string" then return end
	if #name > 200 then return end

	local now = os.clock()
	if lastRequest[player] and now - lastRequest[player] < COOLDOWN then return end
	lastRequest[player] = now

	local blob = DataManager.GetBlob(player, blobId)
	if not blob then return end -- not their blob

	local cleaned = cleanName(name)
	if cleaned == "" then
		blob.Nickname = ""
		return
	end

	local filtered = filterName(player, cleaned)
	if not filtered then return end -- filter service down: keep the old name

	blob.Nickname = filtered
	print(("[BlobNaming] %s named their %s \"%s\""):format(player.Name, blob.Type, filtered))
	task.spawn(DataManager.Save, player)
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	lastRequest[player] = nil
end)

384				d.LocalTransparencyModifier = 1
385			end

388		local keepHidden = RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function()
389			for part in pairs(hidden) do

395		local flatLook = Vector3.new(root.CFrame.LookVector.X, 0, root.CFrame.LookVector.Z)
396		if flatLook.Magnitude < 0.01 then flatLook = Vector3.new(0, 0, -1) end

	local fromCenter = camera.CFrame.Position - orbitCenter
	local radius = math.clamp(fromCenter.Magnitude, ZOOM_MIN, ZOOM_MAX)
	local yaw = math.atan2(fromCenter.X, fromCenter.Z)
	local pitch = math.asin(math.clamp(fromCenter.Y / math.max(fromCenter.Magnitude, 0.01), -1, 1))
	local dragging = false

	local function updateCamera()
		local offset = Vector3.new(
			math.cos(pitch) * math.sin(yaw),
			math.sin(pitch),
			math.cos(pitch) * math.cos(yaw)
		) * radius
		camera.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(orbitCenter + offset, orbitCenter)
	end

			if overGui then return end -- clicks on the card/name box don't drag
			if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
				or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton2
				or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
				dragging = true
			end
		end),
		UserInputService.InputEnded:Connect(function(input)
			if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
				or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton2
				or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
				dragging = false
			end
		end),
		UserInputService.InputChanged:Connect(function(input, overGui)
			if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseWheel and not overGui then
				radius = math.clamp(radius - input.Position.Z * 1.5, ZOOM_MIN, ZOOM_MAX)
			elseif dragging and (input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement
				or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch) then
				yaw -= input.Delta.X * DRAG_SPEED
