--[[
	FarmStations (Script)
	Put this in ServerScriptService.

	Builds and runs each player's farm stations:

	  BERRY GARDEN (outside the plot, in front of the fence left of the gate)
	    • 4 bush spots. Players start with 1 bush; the next spot shows a
	      green pad with its price. Step on it to buy.
	    • Each bush grows 1 berry every GROW_TIME seconds, up to
	      BERRIES_PER_BUSH, even while the player is offline.
	    • Red and Purple bushes can grow rare Silver, Gold or Diamond berries.
	    • Press E / tap a bush to pick its berries.

	  FEEDER (inside the plot, along that same fence)
	    • Press E / tap to put carried berries in (best berries first).
	    • Blobs living on the farm walk over. Once a blob arrives it nibbles,
	      the berry disappears from the trough, and the blob gets its XP.

	  UPGRADE PANELS (on the side wall, left of the feeder)
	    • Feeder: Twig → Wood → Stone → Metal → Gold → Diamond (holds more)
	    • Berries: Red → Purple → Silver → Gold → Diamond (more XP each)

	Short pop-up messages go through Remotes > Notify (shown by FarmHud).
]]

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local DataManager = require(ServerScriptService:WaitForChild("DataManager"))

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SETTINGS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local BUSH_PRICES      = { 0, 50, 200, 500 } -- cost of bush 1, 2, 3, 4 (bush 1 is free)
local GROW_TIME        = 30   -- seconds to grow one berry
local BERRIES_PER_BUSH = 10   -- most berries a bush can hold

-- Berry types, worst to best. Tier = position in this list.
local BERRIES = {
	{ Name = "Red",     XP = 10,  Color = Color3.fromRGB(214, 36, 60),  Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic },
	{ Name = "Purple",  XP = 20,  Color = Color3.fromRGB(140, 60, 205), Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic },
	{ Name = "Silver",  XP = 50,  Color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 210, 220), Material = Enum.Material.Metal },
	{ Name = "Gold",    XP = 100, Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 200, 40), Material = Enum.Material.Metal },
	{ Name = "Diamond", XP = 200, Color = Color3.fromRGB(130, 230, 255), Material = Enum.Material.Neon },
}
-- Cost to upgrade bushes to berry tier 2, 3, 4, 5
local BERRY_UPGRADE_COSTS = { 50, 200, 500, 1000 }

-- Rare berries: only bushes growing Red or Purple roll these (checked rarest first)
local RARE_MAX_TIER = 2
local RARE_CHANCES = {
	{ Name = "Diamond", Chance = 1 / 100 },
	{ Name = "Gold",    Chance = 1 / 50 },
	{ Name = "Silver",  Chance = 1 / 25 },
}

-- Feeder looks. Cost = coins to upgrade TO that tier.
local FEEDERS = {
	{ Name = "Twig Feeder",    Capacity = 10,  Cost = 0 },
	{ Name = "Wood Feeder",    Capacity = 20,  Cost = 50 },
	{ Name = "Stone Feeder",   Capacity = 35,  Cost = 200 },
	{ Name = "Metal Feeder",   Capacity = 50,  Cost = 500 },
	{ Name = "Gold Feeder",    Capacity = 75,  Cost = 1000 },
	{ Name = "Diamond Feeder", Capacity = 100, Cost = 2000 },
}

local EAT_COOLDOWN   = 25  -- seconds before the same blob eats again
local NIBBLE_TIME    = 2.5 -- seconds a blob nibbles before the berry is gone
local EAT_TIMEOUT    = 20  -- if a blob never arrives, it eats anyway after this
local FEED_CHECK     = 3   -- seconds between "who's hungry?" checks

-- Must match PlotManager
local GATE_WIDTH     = 16
local PLATFORM_TOP   = 0.95 -- height of the grey platform (plot-relative)
local GRASS_TOP      = 1    -- height of the plot's grass (plot-relative)

local COLORS = {
	dirt      = Color3.fromRGB(102, 72, 50),
	bush      = Color3.fromRGB(58, 140, 62),
	bushDark  = Color3.fromRGB(42, 110, 48),
	buyPad    = Color3.fromRGB(80, 220, 110),
	panel     = Color3.fromRGB(60, 42, 30),
	panelText = Color3.fromRGB(255, 244, 220),
	accent    = Color3.fromRGB(255, 200, 70),
	text      = Color3.new(1, 1, 1),
}

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SETUP
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local BERRY_BY_NAME = {}
for tier, berry in ipairs(BERRIES) do
	berry.Tier = tier
	BERRY_BY_NAME[berry.Name] = berry
end

local folder = workspace:FindFirstChild("FarmStations")
if not folder then
	folder = Instance.new("Folder")
	folder.Name = "FarmStations"
	folder.Parent = workspace
end

local remotes = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("Remotes")
if not remotes then
	remotes = Instance.new("Folder")
	remotes.Name = "Remotes"
	remotes.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
end
local function getRemote(name)
	local remote = remotes:FindFirstChild(name)
	if not remote then
		remote = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
		remote.Name = name
		remote.Parent = remotes
	end
	return remote
end
local notify = getRemote("Notify")
local atFeeder = getRemote("BlobAtFeeder") -- BlobFollow says "my blob reached the feeder"

local function message(player, text, kind)
	notify:FireClient(player, text, kind or "info")
end

local stations = {} -- [player] = station parts
local pending = {}  -- [blobId] = a blob on its way to / eating at the feeder
local lastAte = {}  -- [blobId] = os.time() it last finished eating
local busy = {}     -- [player] = true while a purchase is being handled

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SAVE HELPERS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function total(berryCounts)
	local n = 0
	for _, count in pairs(berryCounts) do n += count end
	return n
end

-- Brings older saves up to date (numbers → berry types, timers → bushes)
local function migrate(data)
	local farm = data.Farm
	if type(farm.Berries) ~= "table" then farm.Berries = { Red = tonumber(farm.Berries) or 0 } end
	if type(farm.FeederBerries) ~= "table" then farm.FeederBerries = { Red = tonumber(farm.FeederBerries) or 0 } end
	farm.Bushes = farm.Bushes or {}
	if type(farm.BushTimers) == "table" then
		for i, timer in pairs(farm.BushTimers) do
			if not farm.Bushes[i] then farm.Bushes[i] = { Timer = timer, Grown = {} } end
		end
	end
	farm.BushTimers = nil
	farm.BerryTier = farm.BerryTier or 1
	farm.FeederTier = farm.FeederTier or 1
	for i = 1, farm.BushPlots do
		farm.Bushes[i] = farm.Bushes[i] or { Timer = os.time(), Grown = {} }
		farm.Bushes[i].Grown = farm.Bushes[i].Grown or {}
	end
	-- Never more in the feeder than it can hold
	local capacity = FEEDERS[farm.FeederTier].Capacity
	while total(farm.FeederBerries) > capacity do
		for name, count in pairs(farm.FeederBerries) do
			if count > 0 then farm.FeederBerries[name] = count - 1 break end
		end
	end
end

local function syncBerryAttribute(player, data)
	player:SetAttribute("Berries", total(data.Farm.Berries))
end

-- What type of berry a bush grows next
local function rollBerry(berryTier)
	if berryTier <= RARE_MAX_TIER then
		local roll = math.random()
		local chanceSoFar = 0
		for _, rare in ipairs(RARE_CHANCES) do
			chanceSoFar += rare.Chance
			if roll < chanceSoFar then return rare.Name end
		end
	end
	return BERRIES[berryTier].Name
end

-- Adds any berries that have finished growing (works for time spent offline too)
local function growBushes(data)
	local farm = data.Farm
	local now = os.time()
	for i = 1, farm.BushPlots do
		local bush = farm.Bushes[i]
		while #bush.Grown < BERRIES_PER_BUSH and now - bush.Timer >= GROW_TIME do
			table.insert(bush.Grown, rollBerry(farm.BerryTier))
			bush.Timer += GROW_TIME
		end
		if #bush.Grown >= BERRIES_PER_BUSH then
			bush.Timer = now -- a full bush doesn't store up extra time
		end
	end
end

-- Best berry types first
local function bestFirst(berryCounts)
	local list = {}
	for name, count in pairs(berryCounts) do
		if count > 0 and BERRY_BY_NAME[name] then table.insert(list, name) end
	end
	table.sort(list, function(a, b) return BERRY_BY_NAME[a].Tier > BERRY_BY_NAME[b].Tier end)
	return list
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- BUILD HELPERS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function part(props)
	local p = Instance.new("Part")
	p.Anchored = true
	p.TopSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	p.BottomSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	for key, value in pairs(props) do
		if key ~= "Parent" then p[key] = value end
	end
	p.Parent = props.Parent
	return p
end

local function paintBerry(ball, berryName)
	local berry = BERRY_BY_NAME[berryName] or BERRIES[1]
	ball.Color = berry.Color
	ball.Material = berry.Material
	ball.Reflectance = (berry.Tier >= 3 and berry.Tier <= 4) and 0.3 or 0
end

local function billboard(adornee, text, offsetY, width)
	local gui = Instance.new("BillboardGui")
	gui.Name = "Label"
	gui.Size = UDim2.new(0, width or 160, 0, 40)
	gui.StudsOffsetWorldSpace = Vector3.new(0, offsetY, 0)
	gui.LightInfluence = 0
	gui.MaxDistance = 70
	gui.Adornee = adornee
	local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	label.Name = "Text"
	label.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	label.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	label.Font = Enum.Font.FredokaOne
	label.TextScaled = true
	label.TextColor3 = COLORS.text
	label.TextStrokeTransparency = 0.3
	label.Text = text
	label.Parent = gui
	gui.Parent = adornee
	return label
end

local function prompt(parent, action, object, ownerId)
	local p = Instance.new("ProximityPrompt")
	p.ActionText = action
	p.ObjectText = object
	p.HoldDuration = 0
	p.MaxActivationDistance = 10
	p.RequiresLineOfSight = false
	p:SetAttribute("OwnerUserId", ownerId) -- FarmHud hides prompts that aren't yours
	p.Parent = parent
	return p
end

-- The front fence left of the gate, as plot-local X: from the corner to the gate pillar
local function frontLeftRange(plotSize)
	return -plotSize / 2, -(GATE_WIDTH / 2 + 2)
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- BERRY BUSHES
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function bushSpot(plotSize, index)
	local left, right = frontLeftRange(plotSize)
	left -= 2 -- the garden is a little wider than the fence section
	local spacing = (right - left) / 4
	return left + spacing * (index - 0.5), -plotSize / 2 - 6.5
end

-- 10 spots spread over the front and top of the bush
local BERRY_OFFSETS = {}
for i = 1, BERRIES_PER_BUSH do
	local angle = i * 2.4 -- golden-angle spiral so they spread evenly
	local height = 1 - (i - 0.5) / BERRIES_PER_BUSH * 1.5
	local ring = math.sqrt(math.max(0, 1 - height * height))
	BERRY_OFFSETS[i] = Vector3.new(math.cos(angle) * ring, height, math.sin(angle) * ring) * 2.35
end

local refreshStations -- defined below

local function buildBush(player, st, index)
	local x, z = bushSpot(st.plotSize, index)
	local base = st.plotCFrame * CFrame.new(x, PLATFORM_TOP, z)
	local bushModel = Instance.new("Model")
	bushModel.Name = "Bush" .. index
	local center = Vector3.new(0, 2.8, 0)

	part({ Name = "Dirt", Size = Vector3.new(5.2, 0.4, 5.2), CFrame = base * CFrame.new(0, 0.2, 0),
		Color = COLORS.dirt, Material = Enum.Material.Ground, Parent = bushModel })
	local leaves = part({ Name = "Leaves", Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball, Size = Vector3.new(4.6, 4.6, 4.6),
		CFrame = base * CFrame.new(center), Color = COLORS.bush, Material = Enum.Material.Grass,
		Parent = bushModel })
	part({ Name = "Leaves2", Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball, Size = Vector3.new(3.1, 3.1, 3.1),
		CFrame = base * CFrame.new(1.15, 1.8, 0.7), Color = COLORS.bushDark, Material = Enum.Material.Grass,
		CanCollide = false, Parent = bushModel })
	part({ Name = "Leaves3", Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball, Size = Vector3.new(3.1, 3.1, 3.1),
		CFrame = base * CFrame.new(-1.15, 1.8, -0.5), Color = COLORS.bushDark, Material = Enum.Material.Grass,
		CanCollide = false, Parent = bushModel })

	local balls = {}
	for i, offset in ipairs(BERRY_OFFSETS) do
		balls[i] = part({ Name = "Berry", Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball, Size = Vector3.new(0.8, 0.8, 0.8),
			CFrame = base * CFrame.new(center + offset), CanCollide = false, Transparency = 1,
			Parent = bushModel })
		paintBerry(balls[i], "Red")
	end

	local pick = prompt(leaves, "Pick berries", "Berry Bush", player.UserId)
	pick.Triggered:Connect(function(who)
		if who ~= player then return end
		local data = DataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		growBushes(data)
		local bush = data.Farm.Bushes[index]
		if #bush.Grown == 0 then
			message(player, "Not ripe yet. A berry grows every " .. GROW_TIME .. " seconds.")
			return
		end
		if #bush.Grown >= BERRIES_PER_BUSH then
			bush.Timer = os.time()
		end
		local picked, rares = #bush.Grown, {}
		for _, name in ipairs(bush.Grown) do
			data.Farm.Berries[name] = (data.Farm.Berries[name] or 0) + 1
			if BERRY_BY_NAME[name].Tier > data.Farm.BerryTier then
				rares[name] = (rares[name] or 0) + 1
			end
		end
		bush.Grown = {}
		syncBerryAttribute(player, data)
		message(player, ("+%d berries"):format(picked), "good")
		for name, count in pairs(rares) do
			message(player, ("Rare find! +%d %s berr%s"):format(count, name, count == 1 and "y" or "ies"), "rare")
		end
		refreshStations(player)
	end)

	bushModel.Parent = st.model
	st.bushes[index] = { model = bushModel, balls = balls, prompt = pick }
end

-- Only the next bush spot shows a buy pad
local function buildBuyPad(player, st, index)
	local x, z = bushSpot(st.plotSize, index)
	local price = BUSH_PRICES[index]
	local pad = part({
		Name = "BuyPad", Size = Vector3.new(4.6, 0.3, 4.6),
		CFrame = st.plotCFrame * CFrame.new(x, PLATFORM_TOP + 0.15, z),
		Color = COLORS.buyPad, Material = Enum.Material.Neon, Transparency = 0.15,
		CanCollide = false, Parent = st.model,
	})
	billboard(pad, ("Berry Bush\n%d coins"):format(price), 3, 140)

	pad.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
		local character = hit:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
		if not character or Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(character) ~= player then return end
		if busy[player] then return end
		busy[player] = true

		local data = DataManager.Get(player)
		if data and data.Farm.BushPlots == index - 1 then
			if DataManager.SpendCoins(player, price) then
				data.Farm.BushPlots = index
				data.Farm.Bushes[index] = { Timer = os.time(), Grown = {} }
				message(player, "New berry bush planted!", "good")
				task.spawn(DataManager.Save, player)
				refreshStations(player)
			else
				message(player, ("You need %d coins (you have %d)"):format(price, data.Coins), "bad")
			end
		end

		task.wait(2) -- so standing on it doesn't spam messages
		busy[player] = nil
	end)

	st.pad = pad
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- FEEDER (six looks, from twigs to diamond)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local FEEDER_STYLES = {
	-- Twig: crooked sticks lashed together
	{ material = Enum.Material.Wood, color = Color3.fromRGB(112, 80, 52), trim = Color3.fromRGB(86, 60, 38),
		trimMaterial = Enum.Material.Wood, wall = 0.3, twig = true },
	-- Wood: neat planks
	{ material = Enum.Material.WoodPlanks, color = Color3.fromRGB(160, 112, 70), trim = Color3.fromRGB(110, 74, 46),
		trimMaterial = Enum.Material.Wood, wall = 0.3 },
	-- Stone: chunky slate with cobblestone ends
	{ material = Enum.Material.Slate, color = Color3.fromRGB(130, 130, 136), trim = Color3.fromRGB(100, 100, 108),
		trimMaterial = Enum.Material.Cobblestone, wall = 0.5 },
	-- Metal: diamond plate with steel rims
	{ material = Enum.Material.DiamondPlate, color = Color3.fromRGB(150, 160, 172), trim = Color3.fromRGB(96, 104, 116),
		trimMaterial = Enum.Material.Metal, wall = 0.35, rim = true },
	-- Gold: shiny gold with darker gold rims
	{ material = Enum.Material.Metal, color = Color3.fromRGB(240, 190, 50), trim = Color3.fromRGB(200, 145, 30),
		trimMaterial = Enum.Material.Metal, wall = 0.35, rim = true, shine = 0.35 },
	-- Diamond: see-through crystal with glowing rims and sparkles
	{ material = Enum.Material.Glass, color = Color3.fromRGB(150, 230, 255), trim = Color3.fromRGB(120, 220, 255),
		trimMaterial = Enum.Material.Neon, wall = 0.35, rim = true, shine = 0.2, clear = 0.3, sparkle = true },
}

local function feederInfo(plotSize)
	local left, right = frontLeftRange(plotSize)
	return (left + right) / 2, -plotSize / 2 + 2, (right - left) - 3 -- centerX, z, length
end

local function buildFeeder(player, st, tier)
	local style = FEEDER_STYLES[tier]
	local centerX, z, length = feederInfo(st.plotSize)
	local base = st.plotCFrame * CFrame.new(centerX, GRASS_TOP, z)
	local feeder = Instance.new("Model")
	feeder.Name = "Feeder"
	local w = style.wall

	local function piece(name, size, offset, isTrim, extra)
		local p = part({ Name = name, Size = size, CFrame = base * offset,
			Color = isTrim and style.trim or style.color,
			Material = isTrim and style.trimMaterial or style.material,
			Reflectance = style.shine or 0,
			Transparency = (not isTrim and style.clear) or 0,
			Parent = feeder })
		for key, value in pairs(extra or {}) do p[key] = value end
		return p
	end

	local bottom
	if style.twig then
		-- Lumpy floor and walls of thin crooked sticks
		bottom = piece("Bottom", Vector3.new(length, 0.25, 2.2), CFrame.new(0, 0.55, 0), true)
		for row = 0, 2 do
			for _, side in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
				local tilt = (math.random() - 0.5) * 0.12
				piece("Stick", Vector3.new(length + 0.6, 0.3, 0.3),
					CFrame.new(0, 0.8 + row * 0.38, side * 1.05) * CFrame.Angles(tilt, 0, (math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05),
					row % 2 == 1, { Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder })
			end
		end
		for _, side in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
			for _, lean in ipairs({ 0.5, -0.5 }) do
				piece("CrossStick", Vector3.new(2.3, 0.25, 0.25),
					CFrame.new(side * (length / 2), 1.1, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), lean), true,
					{ Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder })
			end
			piece("Leg", Vector3.new(0.4, 0.6, 0.4), CFrame.new(side * (length / 2 - 0.6), 0.3, 0), true,
				{ Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder })
		end
	else
		bottom = piece("Bottom", Vector3.new(length, 0.4, 2.4), CFrame.new(0, 0.6, 0), true)
		for _, side in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
			piece("Side", Vector3.new(length, 1.4, w), CFrame.new(0, 1.1, side * (1.2 - w / 2)))
			piece("End", Vector3.new(w, 1.4, 2.4), CFrame.new(side * (length / 2 - w / 2), 1.1, 0))
			piece("Leg", Vector3.new(0.6, 0.4, 2.4), CFrame.new(side * (length / 2 - 1), 0.2, 0), true)
			if style.rim then
				piece("Rim", Vector3.new(length + 0.2, 0.2, w + 0.2), CFrame.new(0, 1.85, side * (1.2 - w / 2)), true)
			end
		end
	end

	if style.sparkle then
		local sparkles = Instance.new("Sparkles")
		sparkles.SparkleColor = style.trim
		sparkles.Parent = bottom
	end

	-- Berries shown in the trough (up to 15 visible)
	local balls = {}
	for i = 1, 15 do
		local t = (i - 0.5) / 15
		balls[i] = part({ Name = "Berry", Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball, Size = Vector3.new(0.75, 0.75, 0.75),
			CFrame = base * CFrame.new(-length / 2 + 0.8 + t * (length - 1.6), 1.15, (i % 2 == 0) and 0.35 or -0.35),
			CanCollide = false, Transparency = 1, Parent = feeder })
	end

	local label = billboard(bottom, "", 3.2, 190)

	local fill = prompt(bottom, "Add berries", FEEDERS[tier].Name, player.UserId)
	fill.MaxActivationDistance = 12
	fill.Triggered:Connect(function(who)
		if who ~= player then return end
		local data = DataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		local farm = data.Farm
		if total(farm.Berries) <= 0 then
			message(player, "You have no berries. Pick some from your bushes!")
			return
		end
		local space = FEEDERS[farm.FeederTier].Capacity - total(farm.FeederBerries)
		if space <= 0 then
			message(player, "The feeder is full! Upgrade it to hold more.")
			return
		end
		-- Best berries go in first
		local moved = 0
		for _, name in ipairs(bestFirst(farm.Berries)) do
			local amount = math.min(space - moved, farm.Berries[name])
			farm.Berries[name] -= amount
			farm.FeederBerries[name] = (farm.FeederBerries[name] or 0) + amount
			moved += amount
			if moved >= space then break end
		end
		syncBerryAttribute(player, data)
		message(player, ("Added %d berries to the feeder"):format(moved), "good")
		refreshStations(player)
	end)

	feeder.Parent = st.model
	st.feeder = { model = feeder, balls = balls, label = label, prompt = fill,
		centerX = centerX, z = z, length = length, tier = tier }
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- UPGRADE PANELS (on the side wall, left of the feeder)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function buildPanel(player, st, name, zOffset, onUpgrade)
	local half = st.plotSize / 2
	-- Standing against the inside of the left fence, facing into the plot
	local board = part({ Name = name .. "Panel", Size = Vector3.new(0.4, 4.2, 5.6),

local function tryBuy(player, data, cost, onBought)
	if DataManager.SpendCoins(player, cost) then
		onBought()
		task.spawn(DataManager.Save, player)
		refreshStations(player)
	else
		message(player, ("You need %d coins (you have %d)"):format(cost, data.Coins), "bad")
	end
end

local function buildPanels(player, st)
	st.feederPanel = buildPanel(player, st, "Feeder", 6, function()
		local data = DataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		local nextTier = data.Farm.FeederTier + 1
		if not FEEDERS[nextTier] then
			message(player, "Your feeder is fully upgraded!")
			return
		end
		tryBuy(player, data, FEEDERS[nextTier].Cost, function()
			data.Farm.FeederTier = nextTier
			message(player, "Upgraded to the " .. FEEDERS[nextTier].Name .. "!", "good")
		end)
	end)

	st.berryPanel = buildPanel(player, st, "Berries", 12.5, function()
		local data = DataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		local nextTier = data.Farm.BerryTier + 1
		if not BERRIES[nextTier] then
			message(player, "Your berries are fully upgraded!")
			return
		end
		tryBuy(player, data, BERRY_UPGRADE_COSTS[nextTier - 1], function()
			data.Farm.BerryTier = nextTier
			message(player, "Your bushes now grow " .. BERRIES[nextTier].Name .. " berries!", "good")
		end)
	end)
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- KEEP EVERYTHING UP TO DATE
---------------------------------------------------------------------
refreshStations = function(player)
	local st = stations[player]
	local data = DataManager.Get(player)
	if not st or not data then return end
	local farm = data.Farm
	growBushes(data)

	-- Bushes the player owns but that aren't built yet
	for index = 1, math.min(farm.BushPlots, #BUSH_PRICES) do
		if not st.bushes[index] then buildBush(player, st, index) end
	end

	-- Buy pad for the next bush spot only
	local nextIndex = farm.BushPlots + 1
	if st.pad and st.padIndex ~= nextIndex then
		st.pad:Destroy()
		st.pad = nil
	end
	if not st.pad and nextIndex <= #BUSH_PRICES then
		buildBuyPad(player, st, nextIndex)
		st.padIndex = nextIndex
	end

	-- Berries on each bush, in their colors
	for index, bush in pairs(st.bushes) do
		local grown = farm.Bushes[index].Grown
		for i, ball in ipairs(bush.balls) do
			if grown[i] then
				paintBerry(ball, grown[i])
				ball.Transparency = 0
			else
				ball.Transparency = 1
			end
		end
		bush.prompt.ObjectText = ("%s Bush (%d/%d)"):format(BERRIES[farm.BerryTier].Name, #grown, BERRIES_PER_BUSH)
	end

	-- Rebuild the feeder if it was upgraded
	if st.feeder.tier ~= farm.FeederTier then
		st.feeder.model:Destroy()
		buildFeeder(player, st, farm.FeederTier)
	end

	-- Feeder contents: berries stay visible until a blob actually eats them
	local feederInfoTier = FEEDERS[farm.FeederTier]
	local inFeeder = total(farm.FeederBerries)
	local order = {}
	for _, name in ipairs(bestFirst(farm.FeederBerries)) do
		for _ = 1, farm.FeederBerries[name] do table.insert(order, name) end
	end
	local visible = math.min(#st.feeder.balls, math.ceil(inFeeder / feederInfoTier.Capacity * #st.feeder.balls))
	for i, ball in ipairs(st.feeder.balls) do
		if i <= visible then
			paintBerry(ball, order[math.max(1, math.ceil(i / visible * #order))])
			ball.Transparency = 0
		else
			ball.Transparency = 1
		end
	end
	st.feeder.label.Text = ("%s %d / %d"):format(feederInfoTier.Name, inFeeder, feederInfoTier.Capacity)

	-- Feeder upgrade panel
	local fl = st.feederPanel.labels
	local nextFeeder = FEEDERS[farm.FeederTier + 1]
	fl.title.Text = "Feeder Upgrade"
	fl.current.Text = ("%s (holds %d)"):format(feederInfoTier.Name, feederInfoTier.Capacity)
	if nextFeeder then
		fl.nextUp.Text = ("Next: %s, holds %d"):format(nextFeeder.Name, nextFeeder.Capacity)
		fl.cost.Text = ("%d coins"):format(nextFeeder.Cost)
		fl.hint.Text = "Press E to upgrade"
		st.feederPanel.prompt.Enabled = true
	else
		fl.nextUp.Text = "Fully upgraded!"
		fl.cost.Text = ""
		fl.hint.Text = ""
		st.feederPanel.prompt.Enabled = false
	end

	-- Berry upgrade panel
	local bl = st.berryPanel.labels
	local current = BERRIES[farm.BerryTier]
	local nextBerry = BERRIES[farm.BerryTier + 1]
	bl.title.Text = "Berry Upgrade"
	bl.current.Text = ("%s berries (%d XP)"):format(current.Name, current.XP)
	bl.current.TextColor3 = current.Color
	if nextBerry then
		bl.nextUp.Text = ("Next: %s berries, %d XP each"):format(nextBerry.Name, nextBerry.XP)
		bl.cost.Text = ("%d coins"):format(BERRY_UPGRADE_COSTS[farm.BerryTier])
		bl.hint.Text = "Press E to upgrade"
		st.berryPanel.prompt.Enabled = true
	else
		bl.nextUp.Text = "Fully upgraded!"
		bl.cost.Text = ""
		bl.hint.Text = ""
		st.berryPanel.prompt.Enabled = false
	end
end

local function buildStations(player)
	local plotCFrame = player:GetAttribute("PlotCFrame")
	local plotSize = player:GetAttribute("PlotSize")
	local data = DataManager.Get(player)
	if typeof(plotCFrame) ~= "CFrame" or typeof(plotSize) ~= "number" or not data then return end
	migrate(data)

	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = player.Name .. "_Farm"
	model.ModelStreamingMode = Enum.ModelStreamingMode.Persistent

	local st = { model = model, plotCFrame = plotCFrame, plotSize = plotSize, bushes = {} }
	stations[player] = st
	buildFeeder(player, st, data.Farm.FeederTier)
	buildPanels(player, st)
	refreshStations(player)
	model.Parent = folder
	syncBerryAttribute(player, data)
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- FEEDING: farm blobs walk over, nibble, and the berry disappears
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local function reservedCount(player)
	local n = 0
	for _, job in pairs(pending) do
		if job.player == player then n += 1 end
	end
	return n
end

local function finishEating(blobId)
	local job = pending[blobId]
	if not job then return end
	pending[blobId] = nil
	lastAte[blobId] = os.time()

	if job.model.Parent then
		job.model:SetAttribute("GoEat", nil)
		job.model:SetAttribute("EatFacing", nil)
	end

	local player = job.player
	local data = player.Parent and DataManager.Get(player)
	if not data or not DataManager.GetBlob(player, blobId) then return end

	-- Eat the best berry in the feeder
	local best = bestFirst(data.Farm.FeederBerries)[1]
	if not best then return end
	data.Farm.FeederBerries[best] -= 1
	DataManager.AddXP(player, blobId, BERRY_BY_NAME[best].XP)
	refreshStations(player)
end

-- BlobFollow on the owner's screen says the blob has reached the feeder
atFeeder.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, blobId)
	local job = typeof(blobId) == "string" and pending[blobId]
	if not job or job.player ~= player or job.arrived then return end
	if os.clock() - job.startedAt < 0.5 then return end
	job.arrived = true
	task.delay(NIBBLE_TIME, finishEating, blobId)
end)

local function feedBlobs(player)
	local st = stations[player]
	local data = DataManager.Get(player)
	if not st or not data then return end
	local available = total(data.Farm.FeederBerries) - reservedCount(player)
	if available <= 0 then return end

	local blobFolder = workspace:FindFirstChild("ActiveBlobs")
	if not blobFolder then return end
	local now = os.time()

	for _, model in ipairs(blobFolder:GetChildren()) do
		if available <= 0 then break end
		local blobId = model:GetAttribute("BlobId")
		if model:GetAttribute("OwnerUserId") == player.UserId
			and model:GetAttribute("Mode") == "Farm"
			and blobId and not pending[blobId] and data.Blobs[blobId]
			and (not lastAte[blobId] or now - lastAte[blobId] >= EAT_COOLDOWN) then

			available -= 1
			local f = st.feeder
			local x = f.centerX + (math.random() - 0.5) * (f.length - 3)
			local spot = (st.plotCFrame * CFrame.new(x, GRASS_TOP, f.z + 3.2)).Position
			pending[blobId] = { player = player, model = model, startedAt = os.clock(), arrived = false }
			model:SetAttribute("GoEat", spot)
			model:SetAttribute("EatFacing", st.plotCFrame.LookVector) -- face the fence
		end
	end
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- MAIN LOOP
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	local st = stations[player]
	if st then
		st.model:Destroy()
		stations[player] = nil
	end
	busy[player] = nil
	for blobId, job in pairs(pending) do
		if job.player == player then pending[blobId] = nil end
	end
end)

task.spawn(function()
	local feedTimer = 0
	while true do
		task.wait(1)
		feedTimer += 1
		for _, player in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
			if not stations[player] then
				buildStations(player)
			else
				refreshStations(player)
			end
			if feedTimer >= FEED_CHECK then
				feedBlobs(player)
			end
		end
		if feedTimer >= FEED_CHECK then feedTimer = 0 end

		-- A blob that never reached the feeder (stuck, or its owner's game lagged) eats anyway
		for blobId, job in pairs(pending) do
			if not job.arrived and os.clock() - job.startedAt > EAT_TIMEOUT then
				finishEating(blobId)
			end
		end
	end
end)

	if tier <= RARE_MAX_TIER then

All doable, and the effects will stay lightweight. Here's the plan:

- **Upgrade buttons:** the two boards become simple green buttons on the wall that just say **Upgrade Feeder** and **Upgrade Bushes**. The price shows in the little "Press E" prompt when you walk up, so the buttons stay clean. When fully upgraded, a button turns grey.

  - **Gold:** a little golden tree with a trunk
  - **Diamond:** a crystal bush with glowing crystal spikes
- **Eating effect:** when a blob finishes a berry, a small puff of sparkles in the berry's color pops off it, and a **+XP** number floats up and fades, colored by berry type. It's only drawn for players nearby, and it cleans itself up after about a second, so it won't cause lag.

local function berryOffsets(center, radii)
	local offsets = {}

To update: open **FarmStations** in ServerScriptService and replace its code with FarmStations.server.lua. Then open **FarmHud** in StarterPlayer → StarterPlayerScripts and replace it with FarmHud.client.lua. Press Play, and publish with **Alt+P** when you're happy.

Both scripts passed a syntax check. A few things to know:

- **Your bushes are already Diamond**, so you'll see the crystal bushes right away. To see the other four looks, turn on `STUDIO_FRESH_START` (line 53 of DataManager) for a fresh save, then upgrade step by step with your 10,000 test coins. Turn it back off afterward.
- **The garden is now one solid dirt bed** with no gaps, and each bush fills its whole spot.
- **The eating effect is cheap:** one tiny invisible part per bite, 8 to 16 sparkles depending on the berry (Diamond gets the most), and it deletes itself after about a second. Players farther than 80 studs away don't draw it at all.

local function buildButtons(player, st)
	st.feederButton = buildButton(player, st, "Upgrade Feeder", 6, function()
		local data = DataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		local nextTier = data.Farm.FeederTier + 1
		if not FEEDERS[nextTier] then return end
		tryBuy(player, data, FEEDERS[nextTier].Cost, function()
			data.Farm.FeederTier = nextTier
			message(player, "Upgraded to the " .. FEEDERS[nextTier].Name .. "!", "good")
		end)
	end)

	st.bushButton = buildButton(player, st, "Upgrade Bushes", 12, function()
		local data = DataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		local nextTier = data.Farm.BerryTier + 1
		if not BERRIES[nextTier] then return end
		tryBuy(player, data, BERRY_UPGRADE_COSTS[nextTier - 1], function()
			data.Farm.BerryTier = nextTier
			message(player, "Your bushes now grow " .. BERRIES[nextTier].Name .. " berries!", "good")
	-- Upgrade buttons
	local nextFeeder = FEEDERS[farm.FeederTier + 1]
	setButton(st.feederButton, nextFeeder and nextFeeder.Cost, nextFeeder and nextFeeder.Name, "Feeder Maxed")
	local nextBerry = BERRIES[farm.BerryTier + 1]
	setButton(st.bushButton, nextBerry and BERRY_UPGRADE_COSTS[farm.BerryTier],
		nextBerry and (nextBerry.Name .. " Bushes"), "Bushes Maxed")
end

local function buildStations(player)
	local plotCFrame = player:GetAttribute("PlotCFrame")
	local plotSize = player:GetAttribute("PlotSize")
	local data = DataManager.Get(player)
	if typeof(plotCFrame) ~= "CFrame" or typeof(plotSize) ~= "number" or not data then return end
	migrate(data)

	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = player.Name .. "_Farm"
	model.ModelStreamingMode = Enum.ModelStreamingMode.Persistent

	local st = { model = model, plotCFrame = plotCFrame, plotSize = plotSize, bushes = {} }
	stations[player] = st
	buildFeeder(player, st, data.Farm.FeederTier)
	buildButtons(player, st)
	refreshStations(player)
	model.Parent = folder

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- GARDEN FENCE (a short white picket fence around the berry bushes)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local PICKET_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(240, 236, 225)

local function buildGardenFence(st)
	local half = st.plotSize / 2
	local _, right = frontLeftRange(st.plotSize)
	local xLeft, xRight = right - BUSH_SPACING * 4 - 0.25, right + 0.25
	local zNear = -half - 6.5 + BUSH_SPACING / 2 + 0.25 -- side facing the plot
	local zFar = -half - 6.5 - BUSH_SPACING / 2 - 0.25
	local fence = Instance.new("Model")
	fence.Name = "GardenFence"

	-- It's decoration only: players walk straight through it
	local function picket(props)
		props.Color = PICKET_COLOR
		props.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
		props.CanCollide = false
		props.Parent = fence
		return part(props)
	end

	local corners = {
		Vector3.new(xLeft, 0, zNear), Vector3.new(xRight, 0, zNear),
		Vector3.new(xRight, 0, zFar), Vector3.new(xLeft, 0, zFar),
	}
	for i = 1, 4 do
		local a, b = corners[i], corners[i % 4 + 1]
		local length = (b - a).Magnitude
		local dir = (b - a).Unit
		local yaw = CFrame.lookAt(Vector3.zero, dir)
		-- Two rails
		for _, h in ipairs({ 0.45, 0.85 }) do
			local mid = (a + b) / 2 + Vector3.new(0, PLATFORM_TOP + h, 0)
			picket({ Name = "Rail", Size = Vector3.new(0.12, 0.14, length),
				CFrame = st.plotCFrame * (CFrame.new(mid) * yaw) })
		end
		-- Pickets every 1.1 studs
		local count = math.max(2, math.floor(length / 1.1))
		for p = 0, count - 1 do
			local pos = a + dir * (length * p / count) + Vector3.new(0, PLATFORM_TOP + 0.55, 0)
			picket({ Name = "Picket", Size = Vector3.new(0.22, 1.1, 0.22),
				CFrame = st.plotCFrame * (CFrame.new(pos) * yaw) })
		end
	end
	fence.Parent = st.model
end

---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- AUTO FEEDER (Robux game pass)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
local MarketplaceService = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local ROBUX = utf8.char(0xE002) -- shows as the Robux symbol in Roblox text
local studioTestOwners = {}     -- Studio only, before a real game pass ID is set

local function hasAutoFeeder(player)
	return player:GetAttribute("HasAutoFeeder") == true
end

local function checkPassOwnership(player)
	if AUTO_FEEDER_PASS_ID == 0 then
		player:SetAttribute("HasAutoFeeder", studioTestOwners[player] == true)
		return
	end
	local ok, owns = pcall(MarketplaceService.UserOwnsGamePassAsync, MarketplaceService,
		player.UserId, AUTO_FEEDER_PASS_ID)
	player:SetAttribute("HasAutoFeeder", ok and owns or false)
end

MarketplaceService.PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished:Connect(function(player, passId, purchased)
	if passId == AUTO_FEEDER_PASS_ID and purchased then
		player:SetAttribute("HasAutoFeeder", true)
		message(player, "Auto Feeder installed! Thanks for your support!", "good")
		refreshStations(player)
	end
end)

-- A tube (cylinder) between two plot-local points
local function tube(st, parent, a, b, radius, color)
	local worldA = st.plotCFrame * a
	local worldB = st.plotCFrame * b
	local dir = worldB - worldA
	local up = math.abs(dir.Unit.Y) > 0.95 and Vector3.xAxis or Vector3.yAxis
	part({ Name = "Tube", Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder, Size = Vector3.new(dir.Magnitude, radius * 2, radius * 2),
		CFrame = CFrame.lookAt((worldA + worldB) / 2, worldB, up) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0),
		Color = color, Material = Enum.Material.Metal, CanCollide = false, Parent = parent })
	part({ Name = "Joint", Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball, Size = Vector3.new(radius * 2.6, radius * 2.6, radius * 2.6),
		CFrame = CFrame.new(worldB), Color = color, Material = Enum.Material.Metal, CanCollide = false, Parent = parent })
end

local function buildMachine(st, bushCount)
	if st.machine then st.machine:Destroy() end
	local half = st.plotSize / 2
	local _, right = frontLeftRange(st.plotSize)
	local bedNearZ = -half - 6.5 + BUSH_SPACING / 2
	local stripZ = (bedNearZ + (-half - 0.5)) / 2 -- the gap between the garden and the fence
	local boxX = right - BUSH_SPACING * 2 + 0.3
	local feederZ = -half + 2
	local tubeColor = Color3.fromRGB(150, 158, 168)

	local machine = Instance.new("Model")
	machine.Name = "AutoFeeder"

	-- The mechanical box
	local box = part({ Name = "Box", Size = Vector3.new(2.4, 2.6, 2.3),
		CFrame = st.plotCFrame * CFrame.new(boxX, PLATFORM_TOP + 1.3, stripZ),
		Color = Color3.fromRGB(70, 76, 86), Material = Enum.Material.DiamondPlate, Parent = machine })
	part({ Name = "Stripe", Size = Vector3.new(2.5, 0.35, 2.4),
		CFrame = st.plotCFrame * CFrame.new(boxX, PLATFORM_TOP + 0.9, stripZ),
		Color = Color3.fromRGB(245, 196, 40), Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic, Parent = machine })
	part({ Name = "Gauge", Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder, Size = Vector3.new(0.15, 0.8, 0.8),
		CFrame = st.plotCFrame * CFrame.new(boxX, PLATFORM_TOP + 1.7, stripZ - 1.2) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0),
		Color = Color3.fromRGB(235, 235, 235), Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic, Parent = machine })
	local light = part({ Name = "Light", Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball, Size = Vector3.new(0.6, 0.6, 0.6),
		CFrame = st.plotCFrame * CFrame.new(boxX + 0.7, PLATFORM_TOP + 2.75, stripZ),
		Color = Color3.fromRGB(40, 110, 50), Material = Enum.Material.Neon, Parent = machine })

	-- Tube along the garden with a branch into each bush (high enough to clear the picket fence)
	local tubeY = PLATFORM_TOP + 1.9
	local runZ = bedNearZ + 0.9
	local runLeft = right - BUSH_SPACING * (bushCount - 0.5)
	tube(st, machine, Vector3.new(boxX, tubeY, stripZ), Vector3.new(boxX, tubeY, runZ), 0.25, tubeColor)
	tube(st, machine, Vector3.new(math.min(runLeft, boxX), tubeY, runZ),
		Vector3.new(math.max(right - BUSH_SPACING * 0.5, boxX), tubeY, runZ), 0.25, tubeColor)
	for index = 1, bushCount do
		local x = bushSpot(st.plotSize, index)
		tube(st, machine, Vector3.new(x, tubeY, runZ), Vector3.new(x, tubeY, -half - 6.5 + 0.6), 0.2, tubeColor)
	end

	-- Tube up from the box, over the fence, and down into the feeder
	local overY = GRASS_TOP + 6.6
	tube(st, machine, Vector3.new(boxX, PLATFORM_TOP + 2.6, stripZ), Vector3.new(boxX, overY, stripZ), 0.3, tubeColor)
	tube(st, machine, Vector3.new(boxX, overY, stripZ), Vector3.new(boxX, overY, feederZ), 0.3, tubeColor)
	tube(st, machine, Vector3.new(boxX, overY, feederZ), Vector3.new(boxX, GRASS_TOP + 2.2, feederZ), 0.3, tubeColor)

	machine.Parent = st.model
	st.machine = machine
	st.machineLight = light
	st.machineBushes = bushCount
end

-- Moves ripe berries from the bushes into the feeder
local function autoFeed(player)
	local st = stations[player]
	local data = DataManager.Get(player)
	if not st or not data or not hasAutoFeeder(player) then return end
	local farm = data.Farm
	growBushes(data)
	local space = FEEDERS[farm.FeederTier].Capacity - total(farm.FeederBerries)
	local moved = 0
	for i = 1, farm.BushPlots do
		local grown = farm.Bushes[i].Grown
		if #grown >= BERRIES_PER_BUSH then farm.Bushes[i].Timer = os.time() end
		while space - moved > 0 and #grown > 0 do
			local name = table.remove(grown)
			farm.FeederBerries[name] = (farm.FeederBerries[name] or 0) + 1
			moved += 1
		end
	end
	if moved > 0 then
		refreshStations(player)
		-- Blink the light while it works
		local light = st.machineLight
		if light then
			light.Color = Color3.fromRGB(90, 255, 120)
			task.delay(1, function()
				if light.Parent then light.Color = Color3.fromRGB(40, 110, 50) end
			end)
		end
	end
end

-- The green Robux button on the wall
local function buildAutoButton(player, st)
	local btn = buildButton(player, st, ROBUX .. " Auto Feeder", 18, function()
		if hasAutoFeeder(player) then return end
		if AUTO_FEEDER_PASS_ID ~= 0 then
			MarketplaceService:PromptGamePassPurchase(player, AUTO_FEEDER_PASS_ID)
		elseif RunService:IsStudio() then
			-- No game pass yet: free test switch, Studio only
			studioTestOwners[player] = true
			player:SetAttribute("HasAutoFeeder", true)
			message(player, "Studio test: Auto Feeder turned on (free in Studio only)", "good")
			refreshStations(player)
		else
			message(player, "The Auto Feeder isn't for sale yet. Check back soon!")
		end
	end)
	btn.prompt.ObjectText = "Robux game pass"
	st.autoButton = btn
end

local function refreshAutoFeeder(player, st, farm)
	local btn = st.autoButton
	if hasAutoFeeder(player) then
		btn.button.Color = Color3.fromRGB(60, 150, 210)
		btn.edge.Color = Color3.fromRGB(35, 95, 140)
		btn.label.Text = "Auto Feeder ON"
		btn.prompt.Enabled = false
		if not st.machine or st.machineBushes ~= farm.BushPlots then
			buildMachine(st, farm.BushPlots)
		end
	else
		btn.label.Text = ROBUX .. " Auto Feeder"
		btn.prompt.Enabled = true
		if st.machine then
			st.machine:Destroy()
			st.machine = nil
		end
	end
end

content.text: i know little code work for lua the roblox script. i want to make a game let pet peeves on IOS i want to learn how to code a little pet peave that you can ride and shoot poison balls from. jump and make a quick dash as a dodge how hard would that be

chat_messages.text:
It's very doable. I'd rate it beginner-to-intermediate, and a few weeks of learning and tinkering would get you a working version. Each feature is fairly small on its own. The hard part is wiring them together.

**One important thing about iOS:** Roblox Studio, the program you write scripts in, only runs on Windows and Mac. You can't build the game on an iPhone or iPad. Your game will still play fine on iOS once it's published, and Roblox gives you touch buttons for free. If you don't have a computer, a library or school computer works too.

Here's roughly how hard each piece is:

- **Jump:** Very easy. Roblox characters already jump, and if the pet is a Humanoid-based model it works out of the box.
- **Dash/dodge:** Easy-medium. You push the pet forward quickly for a split second, then add a cooldown so it can't be spammed. This is a good first script.
- **Poison balls:** Medium. You spawn a ball, launch it forward, detect when it hits something with the `Touched` event, then apply damage over time to whatever it hit.
- **Riding:** Medium. The easiest method is to put a `Seat` on the pet's back so the player sits on it. Even easier is to make the pet the player's character, so you control it directly.
- **Multiplayer safety:** This is the part beginners usually trip on. Input happens on the player's device (LocalScript), but damage and spawning should happen on the server (Script), and they talk through a `RemoteEvent`. Learn this early.

I'd build it in this order: get a simple pet model moving, then add jump, then the dash, then the poison ball, then the riding. Test each one before moving on.

Here's a tiny dash to get you started. It goes in a LocalScript inside StarterPlayerScripts, and it works on mobile because it creates an on-screen button:

```lua
local ContextActionService = game:GetService("ContextActionService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local canDash = true

local function dash(actionName, inputState)
	if inputState ~= Enum.UserInputState.Begin or not canDash then return end
	canDash = false

	local char = player.Character
	local root = char and char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if root then
		root.AssemblyLinearVelocity = root.CFrame.LookVector * 80
	end

	task.wait(1) -- cooldown
	canDash = true
end

ContextActionService:BindAction("Dash", dash, true, Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift)
ContextActionService:SetTitle("Dash", "Dash")
```

The `true` in `BindAction` is what makes the touch button appear on iOS.

If you'd like, tell me how you want the pet to look (a model you'll make or a free one) and whether you want the player to ride on top or be the pet, and I can help with the next piece.

chat_messages.text:
Here's a full working version: a green ball you ride, steer, and hop on, with a dash dodge and poison shots. It takes two scripts, and the ball builds itself, so you don't need to model anything.

## Setup (in Roblox Studio)

1. In the **Explorer**, hover over **ServerScriptService**, click **+**, and add a **Script**. Paste in Script 1.
2. Hover over **StarterPlayer > StarterPlayerScripts**, click **+**, and add a **LocalScript**. Paste in Script 2.
3. Press **Play**. Walk up to the ball and sit on the seat on top.

## Script 1: Server Script (ServerScriptService)

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")

-- SETTINGS (change these to tune the feel)
local SPEED = 40
local TURN_SPEED = 2.5
local JUMP_POWER = 60
local DASH_SPEED = 120
local DASH_TIME = 0.2
local DASH_COOLDOWN = 1.5
local SHOOT_COOLDOWN = 0.5
local POISON_TICKS = 5
local POISON_DAMAGE = 4
local POISON_INTERVAL = 1

-- Remote so the player's buttons can talk to the server
local remote = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
remote.Name = "BallAction"
remote.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

-- Build the ball
local ball = Instance.new("Part")
ball.Name = "RideBall"
ball.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
ball.Size = Vector3.new(6, 6, 6)
ball.Color = Color3.fromRGB(80, 200, 90)
ball.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
ball.Position = Vector3.new(0, 6, 0)
ball.CustomPhysicalProperties = PhysicalProperties.new(1, 0.1, 0, 1, 1)
ball.Parent = workspace

-- Seat on top (the player sits here)
local seat = Instance.new("VehicleSeat")
seat.Name = "RideSeat"
seat.Size = Vector3.new(2, 0.5, 2)
seat.CFrame = ball.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 3.3, 0)
seat.MaxSpeed = 0
seat.Torque = 0
seat.Parent = workspace

local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
weld.Part0 = ball
weld.Part1 = seat
weld.Parent = ball

-- Keeps the ball upright instead of tumbling
local attachment = Instance.new("Attachment")
attachment.Parent = ball
local align = Instance.new("AlignOrientation")
align.Mode = Enum.OrientationAlignmentMode.OneAttachment
align.Attachment0 = attachment
align.RigidityEnabled = true
align.Parent = ball

ball:SetNetworkOwner(nil) -- server controls the ball

-- State
local yaw = 0
local dashUntil = 0
local lastDash = 0
local lastShot = 0

local function getRider()
	local humanoid = seat.Occupant
	if humanoid then
		return Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(humanoid.Parent), humanoid.Parent
	end
end

local function isGrounded(riderChar)
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { ball, seat, riderChar }
	return workspace:Raycast(ball.Position, Vector3.new(0, -3.6, 0), params) ~= nil
end

-- Driving
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)
	if seat.Occupant then
		yaw -= seat.Steer * TURN_SPEED * dt
	end
	align.CFrame = CFrame.Angles(0, yaw, 0)

	if not seat.Occupant then return end

	local forward = CFrame.Angles(0, yaw, 0).LookVector
	local vel = ball.AssemblyLinearVelocity
	local horizontal

	if os.clock() < dashUntil then
		horizontal = forward * DASH_SPEED
	else
		horizontal = forward * seat.Throttle * SPEED
	end

	ball.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.new(horizontal.X, vel.Y, horizontal.Z)
end)

-- Poison effect
local function poison(humanoid)
	if humanoid:GetAttribute("Poisoned") then return end
	humanoid:SetAttribute("Poisoned", true)
	task.spawn(function()
		for _ = 1, POISON_TICKS do
			if humanoid.Health <= 0 then break end
			humanoid:TakeDamage(POISON_DAMAGE)
			task.wait(POISON_INTERVAL)
		end
		humanoid:SetAttribute("Poisoned", nil)
	end)
end

local function shoot(riderChar)
	local forward = CFrame.Angles(0, yaw, 0).LookVector

	local shot = Instance.new("Part")
	shot.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
	shot.Size = Vector3.new(1.5, 1.5, 1.5)
	shot.Color = Color3.fromRGB(120, 255, 60)
	shot.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
	shot.CanCollide = false
	shot.Position = ball.Position + forward * 5 + Vector3.new(0, 2, 0)
	shot.Parent = workspace
	shot.AssemblyLinearVelocity = forward * 90 + Vector3.new(0, 8, 0)
	Debris:AddItem(shot, 5)

	local used = false
	shot.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
		if used then return end
		if hit:IsDescendantOf(ball) or hit == seat or hit:IsDescendantOf(riderChar) then return end
		used = true

		local humanoid = hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
		if humanoid then
			poison(humanoid)
		end
		shot:Destroy()
	end)
end

-- Handle button presses from the player
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, action)
	local rider, riderChar = getRider()
	if rider ~= player then return end -- only the rider can control it

	if action == "Hop" then
		if isGrounded(riderChar) then
			local v = ball.AssemblyLinearVelocity
			ball.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.new(v.X, JUMP_POWER, v.Z)
		end
	elseif action == "Dash" then
		if os.clock() - lastDash >= DASH_COOLDOWN then
			lastDash = os.clock()
			dashUntil = os.clock() + DASH_TIME
		end
	elseif action == "Shoot" then
		if os.clock() - lastShot >= SHOOT_COOLDOWN then
			lastShot = os.clock()
			shoot(riderChar)
		end
	end
end)
```

## Script 2: LocalScript (StarterPlayerScripts)

```lua
local ContextActionService = game:GetService("ContextActionService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local remote = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BallAction")

local function bindButton(name, title, key, position)
	ContextActionService:BindAction(name, function(_, state)
		if state == Enum.UserInputState.Begin then
			remote:FireServer(name)
		end
		return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink
	end, true, key)

	ContextActionService:SetTitle(name, title)
	ContextActionService:SetPosition(name, position)
end

bindButton("Shoot", "Poison", Enum.KeyCode.E, UDim2.new(1, -90, 1, -220))
bindButton("Dash", "Dash", Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, UDim2.new(1, -170, 1, -150))
bindButton("Hop", "Hop", Enum.KeyCode.F, UDim2.new(1, -90, 1, -110))
```

## Controls

| Action | PC | iOS |
|---|---|---|
| Drive and steer | W/A/S/D | Thumbstick |
| Hop | F | Hop button |
| Dash | Left Shift | Dash button |
| Poison shot | E | Poison button |
| Get off | Space | Regular jump button |

## Notes

- The ball **slides** rather than visually rolling. That keeps the seat upright and steering simple. Once it works, you could put a spinning decorative ball inside it.
- **Tuning:** change the numbers at the top of Script 1. If it feels too floaty, raise `JUMP_POWER` and lower `DASH_TIME`.
- **The server validates everything.** The buttons only send a request, and the server checks that you're really the rider and that cooldowns are up. This stops cheaters from abusing it.
- Poison doesn't stack on the same target, but it restarts after it wears off.

If it doesn't work, tell me what happens (nothing moves, errors in the Output window, buttons missing) and I'll help fix it. Next steps could be making the ball respawn, adding a poison cloud effect, or a health bar for targets.

Thanks for the report. The most likely cause is that Roblox gives the rider's device control of the ball's physics when they sit, which overrides the server's hop and dash. **Controls:** I wasn't sure what "make space jump" meant, since you also asked for Q to jump. I made **Space = Dash**, **Q = Hop**, **E = Poison**, **Shift = Get Off**. To change a key, edit the `Enum.KeyCode` in the LocalScript.

name: Finding the snapping tool in Roblox Studio

chat_messages.text: how to find snapping tool roblox studio

content.text: how to find snapping tool roblox studio

chat_messages.text:
The snapping tools in Roblox Studio are in the **Model** tab (Home tab has some too). Here's where to look:

**Turning on snapping**
1. Open the **Model** tab at the top.
2. In the **Snap to Grid** section, check that **Snap to Grid** is on. This makes Move, Scale, and Rotate jump in fixed steps.
3. Set the step sizes in the boxes next to it: **Rotate** (in degrees) and **Move** (in studs).

**Related tools in the same tab**
- **Align** (Model tab, "Tools" area): lines up selected parts along an axis.
- **Constraints / Snap to Part**: in the Model tab, look for **Part Snap** (also called Surface Snap) in the Tools group, which lets you drag a part so its face snaps to another part's face.
- **Show/Hide Snap Guides**: when dragging with the Move tool, Studio shows snap points on nearby parts if you hold **Ctrl** (Windows) or **Cmd** (Mac) while dragging.

**Tips**
- If you can't see the Model tab, make sure a part or model is selected and you're in Studio's main window, not the Script editor.
- If snapping seems off, check that the step value isn't set to 0 or something very small.
- Menu layouts change a bit between Studio updates, so if a button isn't where I described, try the search bar at the top right of Studio and type "snap."

Which snapping tool are you after: grid snapping, snapping parts to each other, or something else? I can walk through it in more detail.

chat_messages.text: is there an easier way then placing block by block to make a big room

content.text: is there an easier way then placing block by block to make a big room

chat_messages.text:
Yes, a room only takes about 6 parts if you stretch them instead of placing lots of small ones.

**Method 1: Stretch walls (fastest)**
1. Insert one Part (Home tab > Part).
2. Use the **Scale** tool (or set **Size** in the Properties panel, e.g. 40, 1, 40) to make a big floor.
3. Press **Ctrl+D** to duplicate it, then rotate and resize it into a wall (e.g. size 40, 15, 1).
4. Duplicate again for the other walls and the ceiling.

Typing exact numbers into **Size** and **Position** in the Properties panel is the easiest way to get walls that line up perfectly.

**Method 2: Carve a room out of a solid block**
1. Make one large block for the whole room.
2. Make a slightly smaller block and set it inside the first one.
3. Select the smaller block and click **Negate** (Model tab, Solid Modeling group).
4. Select both and click **Union**. The negated block is cut out, leaving a hollow room.

This is also great for doorways and windows: negate a small block where you want the opening, then union it with the wall.

**Method 3: Use plugins or free assets**
- **F3X Building Tools** (free in the Toolbox) is popular for fast resizing, moving, and mirroring.
- The **Toolbox** has modular room and building kits, which are handy if you don't need a custom layout.

**Tips**
- Group finished walls into a **Model** (Ctrl+G) so you can move the whole room at once.
- Turn on **Anchored** for all the parts, or the room will fall apart when you playtest.

Do you want a specific size or style of room, like a house, a dungeon, or an obby lobby? I can suggest exact dimensions.

That prompt almost certainly comes from a **third-party plugin** (or an MCP/AI tool you installed), not from Roblox itself. Roblox doesn't have a built-in Claude connection, so the plugin is asking for your own key so it can call Claude on your behalf.

**If you want to use it**
1. Go to console.anthropic.com and create an account.
2. Add billing or credits. API usage is pay-as-you-go and is separate from a Claude.ai chat account, so a free or Pro chat plan doesn't include a key.
3. Create a key under API Keys and paste it into the plugin.

**Be careful, though**
- Only enter a key into a plugin you trust. Check who made it, its reviews, and how many people use it. A bad plugin could steal the key and run up charges on your account.
- Never put the key in a script inside your game.
- Set a spending limit in the Console so a mistake can't get expensive.

# Building your Roblox dungeon game: roadmap and first lessons

Your idea is a solid one. It's a mix of a "brainrot-style" plot-collection game and a dungeon crawler, and both loops are proven on Roblox. It's a big project for a first game, so I'll break it into small wins you can finish one at a time.

## How long will it take?

These are honest estimates for a complete beginner who is learning as they build:

| Pace | Playable core loop (fight, capture, place on plot) | Full "Part 1" as you described it |
|---|---|---|
| ~5 hrs/week | 3-4 months | 6-9 months |
| ~10 hrs/week | 6-8 weeks | 3-5 months |
| Full-time | 2-3 weeks | 6-8 weeks |

Most of the time goes to learning and debugging, not typing code. Cutting scope is the best way to speed things up. I'd build one hallway, one shop, and one boss room first, then copy and expand them.

## The roadmap

**Phase 1: Learn the basics (1-2 weeks)**
- Install Roblox Studio and learn the interface
- Build simple structures with Parts, Unions, and Models
- Write your first scripts (touch pads, teleporters)

**Phase 2: World and plots (1-2 weeks)**
- Build the surface world and 8 plot areas
- Code the plot claiming system
- Build the tutorial guide

**Phase 3: Combat (2-3 weeks)**
- Wooden sword tool
- Mob AI (goblins and slimes that wander and chase)
- Health, damage, and death

**Phase 4: The core loop (2-3 weeks)**
- Capture the exact mob you killed, with its $ value
- Teleport between the dungeon and the surface
- Place mobs on plot slots (4 at first)
- Mobs earn money, and money is spent in shops

**Phase 5: Dungeon content (3-4 weeks)**
- Hallways, shops, boss rooms, extra loot
- The stairs to level 2, locked until 3 bosses are killed

**Phase 6: Polish (2+ weeks)**
- Saving data, so progress persists between sessions
- Sounds, UI, and testing with friends

## Key design decisions

These will save you a lot of pain later.

1. **Use one Roblox "place" for everything.** Put the dungeon far below or beside the surface, and "teleport" players by moving their position. It's far simpler than linking multiple places.
2. **Keep the important logic in server scripts.** Money, damage, and mob ownership must be handled on the server so exploiters can't cheat.
3. **Use folders and naming conventions from day one.** For example, `Plot1` through `Plot8`, and one template per mob type.
4. **Store mob data as Attributes.** A captured goblin is a model with attributes like `Tier = 1`, `Value = 25`, and `MobType = "Goblin"`. That makes "pick up the exact goblin you killed" easy to implement.

## How the systems will work

- **Plots:** Each of the 8 plots is a Model with a "claim" pad. When a player steps on it, the server sets `Owner = player` and that plot becomes theirs. It has 4 slot parts, and upgrading unlocks more.
- **Mobs:** Templates live in `ServerStorage`. A spawner clones them into the dungeon. A script makes them wander and chase players using `PathfindingService`.
- **Capture:** When a mob's Humanoid dies, you drop a pickup with a `ProximityPrompt` that carries the mob's tier and value. Picking it up stores it in the player's inventory.
- **Teleporters:** A Part with a `Touched` event (or a ProximityPrompt) that moves the player's character to a destination Part.
- **Boss gate:** The server counts each player's boss kills. The stairs check the count before letting them through.

## Lesson 1: Get set up

1. Go to **roblox.com/create**, sign in, and download **Roblox Studio**.
2. Open Studio, choose **All Templates**, then pick **Baseplate**.
3. Find these windows under the **View** tab and make sure they're open: **Explorer**, **Properties**, and **Output**.
   - *Explorer* is the list of everything in your game.
   - *Properties* shows the settings of whatever you've selected.
   - *Output* is where errors and messages appear, so you'll use it constantly.
4. Learn the four essential tools on the **Home** tab: **Select, Move, Scale, Rotate**.
5. Camera controls: hold **right mouse** and move to look around, use **WASD** to fly, and press **F** to focus on a selected object.

**Your first build:** In the **Model** tab, click **Part → Block**. Resize it into a floor 40 studs wide, then add four walls and a doorway. Select everything, press **Ctrl+G** to group it into a Model, and rename it in Explorer. You've just made a tiny room, and your dungeon hallways are built the same way.

## Lesson 2: Your first script (a teleporter)

1. Insert a Part and name it `TeleporterA`.
2. Insert a second Part far away and name it `DestinationA`.
3. Hover over `TeleporterA` in Explorer, click the **+**, and add a **Script**.
4. Paste this:

```lua
local teleporter = script.Parent
local destination = workspace:WaitForChild("DestinationA")

teleporter.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local character = hit.Parent
    local humanoid = character:FindAncestorOfClass("Model") and character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if humanoid then
        character:PivotTo(destination.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 4, 0))
    end
end)
```

5. Press **Play**, walk onto the teleporter, and you should be moved to the destination.

**What it does:** `Touched` fires when something bumps the part. You check whether it was a player (it has a Humanoid), then `PivotTo` moves them. This is the foundation for your surface-to-dungeon teleport, and we'll add a cooldown later so it doesn't fire repeatedly.

## What to do now

- Finish Lessons 1 and 2, and try making a few rooms and a teleporter pair.
- Roblox's free **Creator Hub** tutorials (create.roblox.com/docs) are a good companion. Look for "Beginner scripting" and "Building basics."
- Save your project often (**File → Save to Roblox**).

Once you've done both lessons, tell me how it went, including any errors from the Output window, and I'll walk you through Lesson 3: building the 8 plots and coding the claim system. Do you want to go straight there, or would you like more detail on building structures first (walls, stairs, lighting, and making a dungeon feel atmospheric)?

# Phase 1: Learn the basics

First, a correction. The teleporter script I gave you in Lesson 2 had a bug: one line would have stopped it from ever detecting the player. Use this fixed version instead:

```lua
local teleporter = script.Parent
local destination = workspace:WaitForChild("DestinationA")

teleporter.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local character = hit.Parent
    local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if humanoid then
        character:PivotTo(destination.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 4, 0))
    end
end)
```

Phase 1 has three parts. Do them in order and don't rush. Each ends with a small exercise so you know you've got it.

## Part A: Get comfortable in Studio (Days 1-2)

1. Install Roblox Studio from create.roblox.com and open a **Baseplate** template.
2. Open **Explorer**, **Properties**, and **Output** from the **View** tab.
3. Practice the camera: right-mouse-drag to look, WASD to move, **Shift** to go faster, **F** to focus on a selected object.
4. Practice the tools (Home tab): **Select (Ctrl+1), Move (Ctrl+2), Scale (Ctrl+3), Rotate (Ctrl+4)**.
5. Turn on **snapping**: in the Model tab, set **Rotate Snap** to 15° and **Move Snap** to 1 stud. This keeps walls lined up.

**Two settings beginners always miss**
- **Anchored:** If a Part isn't anchored, it falls or gets pushed around when you press Play. Select your parts and tick **Anchored** in Properties (or click the **Anchor** button in the Model tab). Anchor almost everything you build.
- **Explorer names:** Rename things as you go. `Floor`, `WallLeft`, and `Torch1` are much easier to work with than five parts named "Part."

**Exercise:** Press **Play**, walk around the baseplate, then press **Stop**. Do this after every change you make. Testing often is the most important habit in game dev.

## Part B: Building structures (Days 3-6)

Everything you'll build (hallways, shops, boss rooms) is made from a few simple ideas.

**Parts:** The basic building blocks (Block, Sphere, Wedge, Cylinder). In Properties you can change **Size**, **Color**, **Material** (try Slate, Brick, Cobblestone for a dungeon look), and **Transparency**.

**Models:** Select several parts and press **Ctrl+G** to group them. Now you can move, copy, and reuse them as one object. A hallway is just a model you can duplicate with **Ctrl+D**.

**Wedges and stairs:** Insert a **Wedge** for ramps. For stairs, make one block step, then duplicate it (Ctrl+D) and move it up and forward by a fixed amount, repeating. With snapping on, this is quick. You'll need stairs for the level 2 descent.

**Unions (use sparingly):** Under the **Model** tab, **Union** merges parts, and **Negate** lets you cut holes, such as an arched doorway. Unions are powerful but can be laggy, so only use them for special pieces.

**Lighting for atmosphere:**
- In the **Lighting** service (Explorer), set **Brightness** low and **ClockTime** to 0 or so for a dark dungeon.
- Add a **PointLight** inside a small Part (a torch) for glowing spots.

**Exercises, in order**
1. Build a 40x40 stud room with a floor, four walls, and a doorway.
2. Build a 10-stud-wide hallway about 60 studs long that connects to it.
3. Add a staircase going up 10 studs.
4. Make a torch (a small brown block with a PointLight inside) and place a few along the hallway.
5. Group each piece into a Model and name it (`Room1`, `Hallway1`, `Stairs1`).

By the end of this, you'll have the seed of your first dungeon hallway.

## Part C: Your first scripts (Days 7-12)

Scripts are text files attached to objects. In Explorer, hover over an object, click **+**, and choose **Script**. Any text in `print("...")` shows up in the **Output** window, which is how you check that your code is running.

**Script 1: Hello world**
```lua
print("Hello, dungeon!")
```
Press Play and look in Output. It should appear.

**Script 2: A kill brick** (teaches variables, events, and `if`)
```lua
local brick = script.Parent

brick.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local humanoid = hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if humanoid then
        humanoid.Health = 0
    end
end)
```
**How it works:**
- `local brick = script.Parent` stores the part the script sits inside.
- `brick.Touched:Connect(function(hit) ... end)` means "run this code whenever something touches me."
- `hit` is the specific part that touched it, such as a player's foot.
- `hit.Parent` is the character model, and `FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")` checks whether it's a living character.
- `if humanoid then ... end` only runs the code if that check found something.

**Script 3: A teleporter pair.** Use the fixed script at the top. Set up two Parts, `TeleporterA` and `DestinationA`, with the script inside `TeleporterA`. Make the destination part **Anchored** and put it somewhere far away.

**Script 4: A door that opens** (introduces `ProximityPrompt`, which you'll use for picking up mobs)
1. Insert a Part named `Door` and add a **ProximityPrompt** inside it.
2. Add a Script to the door:
```lua
local door = script.Parent
local prompt = door:WaitForChild("ProximityPrompt")

prompt.Triggered:Connect(function(player)
    door.Transparency = 0.7
    door.CanCollide = false
    task.wait(3)
    door.Transparency = 0
    door.CanCollide = true
end)
```
Press Play, walk up to the door, hold **E**, and it should open for 3 seconds.

**Debugging tip:** If a script doesn't work, check **Output** first. Red text tells you the line number and problem. If nothing appears, add `print("got here")` lines to see how far the script runs. Also check that the script is inside the right object.

## Phase 1 checklist

You're done when you can do all of these without looking anything up:
- [ ] Build and group a room, hallway, and staircase
- [ ] Anchor parts and give them materials and colors
- [ ] Add lights and change the Lighting settings
- [ ] Create a Script and use `print`
- [ ] Explain `Touched`, `if`, and `script.Parent` in your own words
- [ ] Make a working teleporter and a working door

Also try the free **Creator Hub** beginner scripting tutorials at create.roblox.com/docs. They pair well with this and reinforce the same ideas.

When you're through any of these steps, come back and tell me how it went, including any red error text from Output, and I'll help you fix it. Which part do you want to start with, or do you want to jump straight into Part A?

This includes choosing particular proportions, using second base numbers to develop a double-stranded modular scale, and applying the scale’s numbers to specific CSS measurements. He also dives into tactics for determining line-height and line spacing. ... Learn how to define baseline grids, column grids, spacing, and layouts. ... Learn how to create, organize, name, and use icons within a design system. ... Learn about choosing typefaces, font weights, styles, sizes, line-heights, and responsive type for your design system. ... Content and microcopy appear all over design system components.

Typography is arguably the most essential part of any website. When we think about the content of a web page, we think about words. Sebastiano Guerriero breaks down how to think about setting up typographic design systems using CSS globals. From choosing the right font family to creating a modular type scale controlled by variables, this guide walks you through the fundamentals of creating a harmonious set of values for your design system. ... Your mathematics professor was right, you should’ve paid more attention in class! Brent Jackson walks us through designing better typographic systems for the web. By rooting your typographic system in math, you can reduce complexity while maintaining a consistent reading experience that scales across device size. The web lives everywhere from your pocket to your giant desktop monitor, which means your type system needs to strike a balance between consistency and flexibility.

Typography is one of the most important aspects of your design system to establish early on—think of how much information you'll communicate to users through type. Type could account for 85-90% of any given screen. Typography is often one of the foundational components you will want to get a handle on as it will need to work harmoniously with other elements like icons and UI controls. Your line-heights may even influence many other structural elements like spacing and grids. Here are a few key areas you'll want to think through. There are many considerations when choosing typefaces, especially for use on-screen. You may also need to work cross-functionally with brand/marketing teams to accommodate your brand's typefaces and determine how they'll fit into your system. Typefaces can be another touchpoint to help subtly convey the right tone and personality throughout your digital experiences.

If your brand has a very unique typeface, not ideal for extended reading or small sizes, you may opt to reserve it for display sizes for elements like headlines that are used less frequently. In this case, you may want to pair it with a more legible typeface for the bulk of the typography that will appear at smaller sizes. If performance is a critical goal, many design systems will often leverage system/native font-stacks for different platforms to avoid loading web-fonts (as seen in the Shopify Polaris system). Of course, you may also decide to handle these things depending on whether your system needs to support product or a marketing website (where brand personality may be a higher priority). There are many things to factor into your decision, but its a good idea to find the right balance between personality, performance, and on-screen legibility.

Typography · Design Systems · Components · Visual Design · 11K followers · ·Last published Mar 11, 2024 · A collection of stories, studies, and deep thinking from EightShapes · 31K followers · ·252 following · Design systems consultant contributing to the field through the specs plugin, writing and workshops. Everyday digital interfaces include a rich variety of images, visualizations, and other pictures. However, more than anything else, they are made of words. Oh so many words. As we equip teams to design and code usable, consistent, beautiful interfaces using systems, it’s essential that words depend on a strong foundation of typography. I’ll admit, I am not a typography expert. I lack a graphic design degree. I’m never the person choosing a font, scaling type, or finessing letter spacing. As a result, I’ve always been reluctant to write about typography. On the other hand, I am a pattern hunter. Over the years, I’ve contributed to many design systems that set a foundation for typography. Each traversed of steps and decisions to set a foundation and apply it to an emerging library of interface components. This article summarizes those patterns.

From a designer’s perspective, it’s all about downloads. Some fonts are tightly held intellectual property with very intentionally limited sharing. So, at a minimum, a Typography page must provide direct download or instructions on how to get approval to obtain them. Most teams provide a downloadable ZIP that includes all the files you need to install and use fonts locally. For developers, it depends on approach, providing options like: Direct font download to serve the fonts themselves · Instructions for linking to a service like Google Fonts · CDN references that all products refer to collectively · An invitation to contact a technical architect, since a license for the font is required. Organizations requires this to control the recurring and often non-trivial cost of hosting and serving the font. Takeaway: Fonts are needed by different people in different ways.

Most design systems demonstrate a typography scale in documentation as a vertical stack. That’s not enough. A typographic system should also establish constructs like body text, headings, color, responsiveness, color, and other fine-grained details. Systems leverage a type scale to offer core text sizes — often named simply as text or body — that include small, medium, large, and if you need it, xs, xl, and so on. Most systems need three or so (thus, my comfort with using t-shirt sizes). Start with a few and expand as necessary as component designs – and page compositions in the wild. ... Body copy may also offer a distinct “Lead” (alternatively, “Lede”) paragraph to open a page, such as in an article (more on that later). Thus, a simple S/M/L scale may also need other variants lead. This is especially relevant in systems offering multiple sizes, since a Lead for larger, lower density displays would be larger than a Lead for smaller, high density alternatives.

Mastering typography in design systems with semantic tokens and responsive scaling Creating efficient, consistent, and flexible typography for digital platforms using modern design system …

Semantic tokens in typography are design tokens that provide meaning and context to the fundamental typographic properties . They act as an abstraction layer over primitive tokens (which store raw values like font names or sizes), defining how and where these properties should be used within the design system [12] ... A visual representation of semantic typography tokens in a user interface. Using semantic tokens offers several key advantages : Consistency Across Platforms: They ensure that typography remains consistent across different platforms like web, tablet, and mobile, providing a unified user experience . Effortless Updates: Updating typographic styles becomes seamless, as changes to a semantic token automatically apply to all elements using that token. For instance, modifying the font size for all “Bold Heading Large” elements only requires updating the Heading/L/Bold/Size semantic token.

Improving Typography of a Design System As a UX/UI designer in a small design system team supporting dozens of B2B products, I’ve recently had the opportunity to focus on improving our typography …

Semantic tags (<h1>, <h2>, etc.) are HTML elements that help define the page structure and hierarchy, which is crucial for screen readers and SEO. But when we name CSS classes the same way, it implies that the class should always represent that specific level in the hierarchy. This assumption limits the system's flexibility. Instead, major design systems prefer T-shirt sizing (like title-md or title-xl) to keep styling decisions separate from page structure. This approach lets us style typography more fluidly across various use cases without conflicting with page hierarchy requirements. ... Typography is a fundamental aspect of any design system, and scaling it effectively requires balancing consistency, flexibility, and accessibility. Refining it, is an ongoing process, and as needs evolve, having a robust foundation makes adaptation smoother for both designers and developers.

As a UX/UI designer in a small design system team supporting dozens of B2B products, I’ve recently had the opportunity to focus on improving our typography foundations. Managing typography at scale presents unique challenges, especially within an established system where updates often introduce breaking changes. Fortunately, with an upcoming major release, we had the flexibility to refactor and refine some typography elements that were overdue for design and code alignment. In our team, we aim to have one major release each year, allowing for foundational changes like these. Regular releases usually cover enhancements that don’t impact compatibility, keeping day-to-day updates smooth for our adopters · During this refactor, I came across some concepts that I would like to share here: Selecting a font size scale is largely context-driven. Choosing a font size scale depends on the context where will be applied.

Joseph Mueller’s article on Exploring Responsive Type Scales gives helpul guindance on finding the right typography rhythm based on type of project. With our range of B2B products, we prioritize high-density dashboards and data-heavy screens, where legibility is most important. To achieve consistency, we opted for a “Major Second” scale (1.125 ratio), starting with a 14px base font size and scaling up or down by 12.5% increments. ... If you’re wondering why, it’s quite simple, it’s part of the accessibility criteria defined by WCAG (SC 1.4.12). This means a minimum line height of 1.5 times the font size (150%). (font size) * 150% = Line Height Font size = 16px 16 * 150% = 24px · For standard body text, we found this rule effective for readability across various screens. However, for headings, many design systems reduce line height to around 120–130% of the font size to achieve a visually cohesive look.

Build a test environment for the new scale. Check how the new scale affected the UI. Is everything easily readable? Are all the text styles covered by the new scale?
